name: F0001
summary: Syntax error (including Rust syntax that Fascon 1.0 does not have)
detail: A lexical or syntax error (an unterminated string or comment, a malformed integer literal, an unexpected character, chained comparisons such as `a < b < c`, ...). Rust syntax that Fascon 1.0 does not have is reported with this code too: lifetime annotations and char literals (Fascon has no apostrophe token), floating point, generics, `static mut`, and the reserved words `impl`, `enum`, `trait`, `where`, `pub`, `use`, `mod`, `unsafe`, `dyn`, `ref`, `move`, `self`, `extern`, `crate` and `super` (fixed forms such as `extern "C"` declarations excepted). F0001 of 0.1.0 follows the same idea.
constraints: Lifetimes are inferred, so lifetime annotations are never written (references are second-class: arguments and temporary lookups only).
remedy: Just delete lifetime annotations (`fascon explain` shows the source without them and `fascon fix` applies that after verifying it). Write characters as integer codes (`65` and so on), fractions as fixed-point integers, methods as free functions and enums as integer constants or Option. Rust-style code can be converted in one go with automatic reframing (`--reframing=rust`).

name: F0004
summary: Non-exhaustive match
detail: A match does not handle every case (a missing integer value, `Some` / `None`, `Ok` / `Err` or `true` / `false`). A value that matches no arm would leave nothing to do.
remedy: Add the missing arms, or put a `_ => ..` arm last.

name: F0015
summary: A static initializer is not a compile-time constant
detail: The initializer of a static must be a compile-time constant (literals, structs, arrays and expressions over integer statics). Calls and variables are not allowed (the exception is `embed("file")`: F2804).
constraints: Statics live in the Kernel region and are immutable.
remedy: Write the value as a constant. Compute values known only at run time in main and keep them in an arena.

name: F0061
summary: Wrong number of arguments
detail: The number of arguments given to a function, builtin, method or `Some` differs from its declaration. `spawn_on` takes 2 or 3 (core, function[, argument]) and `Some` takes 1. Builtins that take a type or arena name, such as `promote_to_gc`, count that name as an argument. In 0.1.0 this was part of F0308.
remedy: Check the declaration (for a builtin, `fascon dict NAME`) and pass that many arguments.

name: F0062
summary: A field is given twice in a struct literal
detail: A struct literal such as `S { x: 1, x: 2 }` gives the same field twice, so it is unclear which value is meant.
remedy: Delete one of the two.

name: F0063
summary: Missing fields in a struct literal
detail: A struct literal `S { .. }` leaves out some declared fields. Fascon has no default values and never creates uninitialized memory.
remedy: Give every field a value (`None` for Option fields, `0` for integers).

name: F0069
summary: A return without a value
detail: `return;` was written in a function that has a result type.
remedy: Write `return value;`.

name: F0070
summary: Assignment to something that is not a place
detail: The left side of an assignment is not a variable, a field or an index (`a[i]`, `a[id]`) but some other expression, such as a call result or a calculation.
remedy: Assign to a variable, a field or an index.

name: F0107
summary: Wrong type arguments
detail: `Result<T, E>` takes two types, `Option<T>` one type, and `Id<@name>` and `Dma<@name>` one arena name. Other types take no arguments (an alias `type Name<@a: T>` takes as many as it declares).
constraints: There are no generics, so only these builtin types and aliases take arguments.
remedy: Write the type arguments in the forms above.

name: F0124
summary: A struct declares a field twice
detail: A `struct` declaration has two fields with the same name.
remedy: Rename one of them.

name: F0268
summary: break / continue outside a loop
detail: `break` and `continue` can only be written inside `loop`, `while` or `for`.
remedy: Move it into a loop, or use `return` to leave the function.

name: F0277
summary: The value in `[value; N]` cannot be copied
detail: The value of an array repeat expression `[value; N]` must be copyable (integers, bool, Id, Str, ...) or `None`. A value that contains own cannot be duplicated N times.
remedy: Create it with `[None; N]` and fill the elements one by one, or write each element.

name: F0308
summary: Type mismatch
detail: The expected type and the actual type differ. This also covers integer literals and patterns out of the range of their type, a function that must return a value but does not, `main` or a builtin used as a value, indices, shift amounts or ranges that are not integers, function pointer types that differ in reference mutability (`fn(&i32)` is not `fn(&mut i32)`), and a `&` added to a by-value argument or missing from a reference argument. In 0.1.0 exhaustiveness and argument counts were part of this code; in 1.0 they are F0004 and F0061.
constraints: Integers are never converted implicitly (use `as`).
remedy: Make the types agree: convert with `as`, add a type annotation, match the `&` / `&mut` of arguments to the declaration, or end the function with a value.

name: F0317
summary: An if without else used as a value
detail: A value was taken from an `if` without `else`, as in `let x = if c { 1 };`. There is no value when the condition is false.
remedy: Add an `else` and produce a value of the same type in both branches.

name: F0368
summary: A compound assignment on an unsuitable type
detail: A compound assignment such as `+=`, `-=` or `<<=` was used on a type without that operation (bool, Str, a struct, an Option, an Id, ...).
remedy: Use it on integer variables and fields. For other types, build the value you mean and assign it with `=`.

name: F0369
summary: An operator that the type does not support
detail: A binary operator was used on a type that does not support it: comparing values that cannot be compared (structs, Options, own, ...), shifting something that is not an integer, adding bools, and so on.
remedy: Compare fields, examine Options with `match` / `if let`, or convert to integers with `as`.

name: F0381
summary: Use of a possibly-uninitialized variable
detail: A variable declared without a value (`let x;`) is used although some path leaves it unassigned (for example, only one branch of an if assigns it).
constraints: Fascon never lets a program read uninitialized memory.
remedy: Give it a value when declaring it, or assign it in every branch.

name: F0382
summary: Use after move
detail: `own T` (and values containing own) are move-only: passing by value, assignment, a `spawn_on` argument and a channel `send` move the ownership. The variable was used again after the move (further down in program order). Moving in only some arms of a match and using the value after the match is still F0382 (union rule). A move inside a loop is F0382 when the next iteration uses it.
constraints: There are no implicit copies. A moved variable cannot be used until it is assigned again.
remedy: Move it after its last use, pass a reference (`&x`), or clone it explicitly with `.clone()`. `fascon explain` shows the timeline from the move to the use.

name: F0384
summary: Assignment to an immutable place
detail: An assignment to a `let` variable without `mut` (a part of it or the contents of its own included), a second assignment to an immutable variable that already has a value, or an assignment to a static (statics live in the Kernel region and are immutable).
constraints: There is no `static mut` (shared mutable state is an arena or an MMIO region).
remedy: Declare it with `let mut`. Keep shared state in an arena.

name: F0391
summary: A cyclic definition
detail: The initializer of a static depends on itself (possibly through other statics), or a type alias `type` contains itself.
remedy: Break the cycle: write one side as a constant, or spell the alias out as a real type.

name: F0412
summary: Unknown type
detail: The name of a type (a struct, an alias or a builtin type) cannot be found. Usually a typo.
constraints: The builtin integer types are `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`, `usize`, `i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64` and `isize`; there are also `bool`, `Str`, `Option`, `Result` and `Id`.
remedy: Check the spelling, or declare `struct Name { .. }`.

name: F0415
summary: A parameter is declared twice
detail: A function has two parameters with the same name.
remedy: Rename one of them.

name: F0422
summary: Unknown struct
detail: The name in a struct literal `Name { .. }` is not a declared struct.
remedy: Check the spelling, or declare `struct Name { .. }`.
aliases: 構造体が見つからない

name: F0423
summary: A type name used as a value
detail: Only the name of a struct type was written where a value belongs (`let b = Button;`).
remedy: Write a struct literal: `Button { label: "OK", x: 1 }`.

name: F0425
summary: Unresolved name
detail: The name of a variable, function, static or region cannot be seen from that place (a typo, a variable of another block, an undeclared function, ...). Type names are F0412 and struct literal names are F0422.
constraints: A variable is visible only inside the block that declares it. Functions, statics and regions can be used regardless of the order of declarations.
remedy: Check the spelling and the scope. Look builtins up by name (for example `fascon dict timer_arm`).

name: F0428
summary: A name is defined twice
detail: A function, static, type or region (arena, mmio, port_io, ...) with the same name is defined twice. Regions are used by their bare name, so a region cannot share its name with a function, static or type either.
remedy: Rename one of them.

name: F0435
summary: A non-negative integer known at compile time is required
detail: Arena and channel capacities, MMIO addresses, port numbers and the size and virtual address of user memory must be non-negative integers known at compile time (variables and call results are not allowed).
remedy: Write a literal, or a constant expression over integer statics.

name: F0499
summary: The same place is mutably borrowed twice in one call
detail: The arguments of one call borrow the same place (or part of it) twice with `&mut`. Two slots of one arena (`&mut a[x], &mut a[y]`) count too, because the Ids may be equal. References are second-class, so a borrow exists only during the call and conflicts are decided statically within that call.
constraints: At any point there is at most one mutable borrow of a place.
remedy: Split the call, or pass different fields (`&mut a.x, &mut a.y` is fine). For two arena slots, read the values out and write them back.

name: F0502
summary: An access that conflicts with a borrow
detail: A place was read, written or borrowed while it is borrowed. Borrows come from `&mut` arguments of a call (for that call) and from bindings, lookups and views such as `if let Some(n) = list.head` (until the end of that block). For example, replacing the own that n points at with `list.head = None;` inside the same block is F0502. For arena slots the code is F2502.
constraints: A mutably borrowed place cannot be read, and a borrowed place cannot be written.
remedy: Copy the value into a temporary before the call (`let tmp = a.x; f(&mut a, tmp);`). Write the place after the block of the binding ends.

name: F0505
summary: Move while borrowed
detail: Ownership of a value that is being borrowed was moved: either a borrow and a move overlap in the arguments of one call, or the original value is moved (`let moved = b;`) inside a block where a view (`view` / `view_mut`) or a lookup binding is still alive.
remedy: Move it after the borrow ends (after the block), split the call, or `.clone()` one side.

name: F0507
summary: Move out of a field, referent, static or own contents
detail: Ownership was taken out of a struct field, a referent (`*r`) or a static (partial moves are forbidden). This includes replacing an own through a binding of the own place (`match w.ok { b => .. }`, `if let Some(b) = w.status`): like `&mut w.ok`, the binding refers to the contents of the own. It also includes taking a non-copyable value (a struct, a Str, ...) out of the contents of a non-struct own (`*b`) and moving an own field out (`let b = ctx.buffer;`), since either would leave the own empty.
constraints: There are no implicit copies.
remedy: Clone explicitly with `.clone()`. To replace an own, assign the original place (`w.ok = own Button { .. }`). Read the contents of an own as a copy with `*b` (`let v = *ctx.buffer;`), or move the whole own (without `*`).

name: F0515
summary: Second-class reference violation
detail: A reference `&T` / `&mut T` (windows `&[u8]` and the results of lookups such as `get` and `view` included) was put somewhere other than a function parameter: a let binding, a struct field, a result, the contents of an Option, Result or own, an arena or channel element, a static, another core, or a reference to a reference. `&x` can only be created as a call argument, and a lookup result can only be the scrutinee of `if let` / `match` or a place followed by `.unwrap()`.
constraints: A reference exists only as a function argument and its lifetime is confined to that call (which is why no lifetime annotations are needed).
remedy: Own the value (keep it in a struct field or behind an Id), or pass it directly as `f(&x)`. Use lookups inside `if let Some(v) = a.get(id) { .. }`.

name: F0596
summary: Writing or mutably borrowing a read-only place
detail: A read-only place was written or borrowed with `&mut`: the target of a shared reference `&T`, a read-only lookup such as `.get(id).unwrap()`, a variable without `mut`, a static, or read-only bytes. Passing a shared reference to a `&mut T` parameter, passing a `&mut` parameter without `&mut`, and `.take()` on a read-only place are included.
remedy: Declare it with `let mut`, make the parameter `&mut T`, or write through `.get_mut(id)` (or `a[id]`).

name: F0599
summary: No such method
detail: A method that the kind of value does not have was called. Fascon has no user-defined methods (`impl`); only the methods of builtin kinds exist: arenas, channels (`send(value)` / `recv()` / `recv_wait()`; channels cannot be indexed), `dma` regions (`phys` / `len`), user memory (only `of(task_id)`), ports (`read` / `write` / `read_at` / `write_at`), MMIO regions and so on. A method of process tables used on another arena is included. The message lists, in parentheses, the methods that value has. 0.1.0 had far fewer builtin methods, so the meaning is wider now.
constraints: There are no impl blocks.
remedy: Write a free function `fn f(x: &T)` and call it as `f(&x)`. For builtin kinds, use one of the methods listed in the message.

name: F0600
summary: A unary operator that the type does not support
detail: Unary `-` on an unsigned integer (`u8` to `u64`, `usize`), or `-` / `!` on something that is neither an integer nor a bool.
remedy: Convert to a signed type first (`-(x as i64)`). Examine Options and the like with `match` / `if let`.

name: F0601
summary: `fn main()` is missing or has the wrong shape
detail: Execution starts at `fn main()`. main is missing, or it has parameters or a result.
remedy: Write `fn main() { .. }` with no parameters and no result.

name: F0605
summary: A cast that `as` cannot do
detail: `as` only converts numbers (integer to integer, bool to integer, ...). Structs, Options, Str, references and own cannot be cast. Use `*` to read the contents of an own.
remedy: Use `as` for numeric conversions only. Read own contents with `*b`.

name: F0608
summary: Not indexable, or a constant index out of bounds
detail: Indexing `x[i]` was used on something that cannot be indexed (read a Str with `s.byte(i)`, read and write a non-array port by its name, the number of dimensions differs), or an index known at compile time is beyond the length of the array (F2201 for fixed-address regions).
constraints: Indices known only at run time are bounds-checked; the check is dropped when the range is proven.
remedy: Use `s.byte(i)` for Str, port names for ports, and keep constant indices inside the length.

name: F0609
summary: No such field
detail: `.name` was read on a type without fields (an integer, an Option, ...) or on a struct that has no such field.
remedy: Match the spelling to the declaration. Take the value out of an Option with `if let Some(v) = ..` first.

name: F0728
summary: Await outside async
detail: `.await` was used outside an async fn.
remedy: From synchronous code, use `block_on(f(..))`.

name: F0808
summary: Region containment failure
detail: No region can be statically proven to contain the value's lifetime. Examples: holding a reference argument (the caller's Thread/Call region) across .await, capturing a reference argument in spawn, moving a caller's value (an argument) to another thread as is, replacing a whole referenced object.
constraints: There is never an implicit global promotion (hiding the value in a static area); the build is rejected instead.
remedy: Quick Fix: make the data an owned value that moves into the task / thread, rewriting the allocation so that it is promoted to a Process (or Kernel) class region (`&T` → `T`, and `.clone()` at the call site).

name: F0810
summary: Unbounded loop allocation
detail: In a loop whose iteration count is not statically bounded (loop / while / for over a non-constant range), an allocation is promoted to a loop-carried variable, the caller or a shared region, so the outer region grows on every iteration. Even if the requirement sets of the backward fixpoint analysis converge, the region increment Grow(n+1)−Grow(n) > 0 remains, so no fixpoint exists. The typical case is `head = Node { next: Some(head) }`.
constraints: `for i in 0..N` over a constant range is bounded and allowed (promoted outward). An allocation right before leaving (just before return/break) happens once and is allowed.
remedy: Quick Fix: find where the loop forms a recursive link, lift the allocation site out of the loop (into the Call region) and turn the loop body into an in-place update. If it only escapes when leaving, use `return x.clone()`.

name: F0811
summary: volatile_bypass violation
detail: Inside `volatile_bypass { .. }` there is an own allocation, a function call or an arena operation, or `mmio_read` / `mmio_write` and the like are used outside it.
constraints: volatile_bypass is a section for raw address accesses only, so nothing that affects region analysis may be placed in it.
remedy: Allocate and call outside, and keep only integers and `mmio_*` inside. A type-safe `mmio name: [u32; N] at address;` needs no volatile_bypass and is bounds-checked.

name: F0900
summary: Isr region capacity exceeded
detail: The static upper bound (Σ count × size) of the allocations reachable from an interrupt handler exceeds the Isr capacity (1 KB by default), or there is no bound (allocation inside recursion or an unbounded loop). Exceeding the capacity at run time is an immediate panic (fascon_plat_kernel_panic(0x0900)).
constraints: The Isr region is pre-allocated statically for each CPU and cannot move to another CPU.
remedy: Reduce the allocations in the ISR or increase `--isr-capacity`. Place the Isr pool in TCM/SRAM with a linker script (gen-ld).

name: F0901
summary: Forbidden operation in an interrupt handler
detail: spawn / send / recv / block_on / await / channel creation was used in an #[isr] function (or a function called from it).
constraints: Operations that may block and thread operations are forbidden in interrupt context.
remedy: Move the work to normal context.

name: Second-class reference
summary: A reference can exist only as a function argument
detail: `&T` / `&mut T` can only be written as the type of a function parameter. The caller creates it directly as an argument in the form `f(&x)` / `f(&mut x)`. This confines the lifetime of every reference to the duration of that call, so no lifetime annotation ('a) is ever needed.
constraints: Do not bind it with let, store it in a struct, return it, put it into an Option/channel, capture it in spawn (F0808) or hold it across .await (F0808). Passing a reference argument on to another function as is (reborrowing) is allowed.
remedy: Keep values that must live long as owned values. To share, .clone() them or send them through a channel together with ownership.

name: Borrow rules
summary: Mutable / immutable borrow rules within one call (F0499 / F0502 / F0505)
detail: With second-class references a borrow exists only inside a call expression, so conflicts can be decided statically among the arguments of the same call. Non-overlapping fields can be borrowed at the same time (`f(&mut p.x, &p.y)` is allowed).
constraints: Only one &mut to the same place; &mut cannot coexist with & / a read / a move.

name: Kernel
summary: System-persistent, accessible from all CPUs, immutable
detail: Static structs and channels live here. In the generated code they are placed in the .fascon_kernel section (cache-line aligned) and become immutable after initialization with fascon_kernel_seal(). Values sent to a Kernel channel are allocated in a Promoted(Kernel) transfer region.
constraints: Exceeding the limit is a system panic. static mut is forbidden.

name: Process
summary: Unit of space isolation, shared by several threads (Process/Task category)
detail: Values that cross a thread boundary (spawn capture / send) are allocated as Promoted(Process) in a Process-class transfer region (xfer) that can be handed over together with ownership. The receiver adopts it into its own region and reclaims it in bulk when the receiver frees it. Channel bodies live in the process-shared region.
constraints: Allocations are aligned to the cache line (alignas(64)). Allocations in the shared region are synchronized with a mutex (spin lock).

name: Task
summary: Values that live across await points (Process/Task category)
detail: Values required across .await in the backward analysis are marked RegionClass::Task and allocated in the Task region created by block_on. They are reclaimed in bulk when the task ends.
constraints: Holding a reference argument across await is F0808. In v0.1.0, await is lowered to synchronous execution (run-to-completion).

name: Thread
summary: Unit of thread execution, exclusive to one thread (no synchronization needed)
detail: Holds the values of a spawn body and the captures it received (adopted transfer regions). Freed in bulk when the thread ends.

name: Call
summary: One region per call (O(1) bump allocation, bulk free)
detail: A region for each function call. fascon_region_cleanup is inserted at the end of the function and before every early return. The return value is allocated directly in the caller's region (the hidden first parameter __parent_reg), a static promotion to Parent. Temporaries inside loops are placed in an iteration region that is bulk-freed every iteration.

name: Isr
summary: Dedicated to interrupt handlers, pre-allocated statically per CPU
detail: Allocations inside #[isr] functions are O(1) bumps from a CPU-local Isr pool; when the interrupt returns, the bump position is restored, freeing everything at once (nesting supported, no atomic instructions). The Isr pool can be pinned to TCM / scratchpad SRAM / a cache-locked area with a linker script.
constraints: It cannot move to another CPU. Exceeding the capacity (1 KB by default) is an immediate panic, F0900.

name: Requirement set
summary: requirements: the set of variables / paths required after a given point
detail: MasSemaAnalyzer scans the code from back to front and computes the requirement set at each point. A use adds, let and assignment to a whole variable (strong update) remove, and a move adds as a use.

name: Backward fixpoint analysis
summary: Pass 1 (mas-sema-analysis)
detail: Runs the backward data-flow analysis to a fixpoint around loops. Requirement sets grow monotonically and are finite, so it always converges. In loops it separates per-iteration temporaries from values that live across iterations and promotes the latter to the outer region. A region increment that does not converge is F0810.

name: Union rule
summary: The requirement set before a match / if = the union of the arms' requirement sets
detail: Saves the requirements right before entering the match as the base, restarts each arm from the base and scans it backward, then combines the arms' results as a union that replaces the requirement set before the whole match.

name: Strong update
summary: let / assignment to a whole variable removes the name from the requirement set
detail: A rebound variable is a different value, so after a move, rebinding with `let x = ...` makes later uses no longer F0382.

name: Promotion
summary: Static promotion
detail: Promotes the region of an allocation site upward to match its lifetime: return value → Parent, crossing threads → Promoted(Process/Kernel), across await → Task, across loop iterations → outer. When it cannot be analyzed, there is no implicit global promotion: it is F0808.
remedy: `fascon regions <file>` shows the region chosen for each allocation.

name: Pass 2
summary: mas-sema-apply: region assignment (destructive transform)
detail: Groups allocation sites and variables into region equivalence classes with union-find and decides the destination of each class (Call / iteration / Parent / Process / Kernel / Task / Thread / Isr). Function summaries handle the flow from arguments to return values across calls.

name: Affine ownership
summary: A struct / Option<struct> can be moved at most once
detail: Integers, bool, Chan handles and shared references are Copy. Structs are owned values that cannot be used after a move. Copies are made explicitly with .clone().
constraints: Implicit copies are forbidden.

name: fn
summary: Function definition (hidden parameters __parent_reg / __ctx are inserted automatically)
detail: In C it becomes `T f(FasconRegion* __parent_reg, FasconCtx* __ctx, ...)`. Lifetimes, regions and allocator arguments are never written.

name: let
summary: Variable binding (strong update)
detail: `let mut` makes it mutable. References cannot be bound (F0515).

name: match
summary: Branching (analyzed with the union rule)
detail: Integer, bool, Option (Some(x) / None) and `_` patterns. It must be exhaustive. The x in Some(x) is an alias of the scrutinee: moving x also moves the original value.
constraints: match guards are not supported.

name: loop
summary: Infinite loop (iteration count is not bounded)
detail: If an allocation inside the loop is promoted outward, it is F0810.

name: for
summary: Range loop `for i in a..b`
detail: If a and b are integer literals, it is treated as a bounded loop and promotion outward is allowed (no F0810).

name: return
summary: Early return (fascon_region_cleanup is always inserted right before it)
detail: The return value is already allocated in __parent_reg, so it survives when the Call region is freed.

name: struct
summary: Struct (an owned value allocated in a region)
detail: Types allocated in Process/Kernel/Task/transfer regions get _Alignas(FASCON_CACHE_LINE) on their first member, and their sizeof becomes a multiple of the cache-line size.
constraints: A self-referencing field must be Option<Self>. Reference fields are not allowed.

name: static
summary: Immutable data in the Kernel region
detail: Integers, bool, struct literals and chan(N) can be used as initializers. `const` means the same.
constraints: static mut is forbidden. Use .clone() to move out of a static.

name: async
summary: Asynchronous function (Task region)
detail: In C it has a third parameter __task_reg. Call it with `.await` / `block_on`. In v0.1.0, await runs synchronously.

name: spawn
summary: Thread creation `spawn { ... }` (move capture)
detail: Outer variables used by the body move together with their ownership and are adopted into the new thread's Thread region through a Promoted(Process) transfer region. Integers and Chan are copied.
constraints: Capturing a reference argument is F0808. Reusing a value after the move is F0382.

name: volatile_bypass
summary: Direct physical-address access block (completely isolated from and exempt from region analysis)
detail: Reads and writes MMIO such as an APIC or UART with mmio_read*/mmio_write*. In C it is wrapped in FASCON_BYPASS_ENTER/EXIT (barriers), and every access is volatile with an I/O barrier (AArch64: dmb oshst/oshld, RISC-V: fence w,o / i,r).
constraints: Allocations, moves, user function calls and channel operations are forbidden inside it (F0811).

name: #[isr]
summary: Interrupt handler attribute
detail: In C it becomes `void fascon_isr_<name>(void)` and is called from the BSP's interrupt vector. Allocations inside it use the Isr region.
constraints: No parameters, return value or async. spawn/send/recv/await are not allowed (F0901).

name: Some / None
summary: Values of Option
detail: Option<struct> is a nullable pointer in C; Option<integer> is an {is_some, value} struct.

name: chan
summary: A channel that passes values between cores (the SMP extension of Fascon 1.0)
detail: `chan work: own Packet[8];` is a lock-free ring buffer (the capacity is a power of two). `work.send(value)` moves the value in (waiting while the channel is full; the sent variable can no longer be used: F0382), `work.recv()` gives an `Option` (None when empty) and `work.recv_wait()` waits until a value arrives. It also works in programs that do not use `spawn_on` (on one core). For channels that can carry Ids of a shared gc_arena, elements not yet received are GC roots. `chan` is not a reserved word, and it is unrelated to the 0.1-only `chan::` syntax.
constraints: F2615: the capacity is not a power of two (2 to 65536), or the element is neither `own T` nor a value that needs no drop. F0515: references and function pointers cannot be elements (they cannot cross cores). F2603: on multi-core, `send` / `recv_wait` (operations that wait) cannot be used inside `critical`. F2803: not available in user programs.

name: send
summary: `ch.send(v)` sends together with ownership
detail: A struct is sent together with its transfer region (v cannot be used after sending).

name: recv
summary: `ch.recv()` receives (blocking)
detail: The received transfer region is adopted into the region of the receiving variable.

name: clone
summary: `.clone()` explicit deep copy
detail: The destination region is inferred from how the copy is used (Process if it is sent to a thread).

name: block_on
summary: `block_on(f(..))` runs an async fn from synchronous code
detail: Creates a Task region and reclaims it in bulk when the task ends.

name: print_int / print_str
summary: Print an integer / a string literal
detail: Through fascon_plat_print (BSP). Does not depend on libc.

name: panic
summary: `panic("..")` safe stop
detail: Calls fascon_plat_kernel_panic(FASCON_PANIC_USER).

name: mmio_read / mmio_write
summary: `mmio_read32(addr)` / `mmio_write32(addr, v)` (8/16/32/64)
detail: volatile access plus an architecture-specific I/O barrier.
constraints: Usable only inside volatile_bypass (F0811).

name: fence / compiler_fence
summary: Full hardware fence / compiler barrier
detail: fence(): mfence / dmb ish / fence rw,rw. compiler_fence(): asm volatile("" ::: "memory").

name: cpu_id / cpu_relax
summary: Current CPU number / spin-wait hint (pause / yield)

name: Integer types
summary: i8 i16 i32 i64 isize u8 u16 u32 u64 usize
detail: Arithmetic is checked (overflow, division by zero and out-of-range shifts panic safely). No C undefined behavior is generated. The type of an integer literal is inferred from its use (i32 by default).
constraints: Floating point is not supported in v0.1.0.

name: Option<T>
summary: A type that may or may not hold a value
constraints: Nested Options are not supported.

name: Chan<T>
summary: Channel handle (Copy)
constraints: References cannot be sent.

name: Cache-line alignment
summary: Removing false sharing with alignas(64) / padding
detail: When different CPUs frequently write different variables on the same 64 B line, the line keeps being invalidated and transferred and saturates the bus even without locks. codegen.rs puts _Alignas(FASCON_CACHE_LINE) on the first member of structs used in Process / Kernel / Task / transfer regions and pads sizeof to a multiple of the line size. The runtime also gives each per-CPU structure, CAS list head and lock its own line.
constraints: Use `--cache-line 128` to account for Apple M-series or Intel adjacent-line prefetching. Cortex-M7/R5 use 32 B.
aliases: キャッシュラインアライメント

name: Memory barriers
summary: Preventing reordering at compile time and at run time
detail: The generated code puts FASCON_BOUNDARY_FENCE (asm volatile("" : : "r"(reg) : "memory")) before and after fascon_region_cleanup, so GCC can neither remove the cleanup nor reorder accesses to the region. Hand-offs between CPUs (channels, the CAS free list, transfer regions) guarantee visibility with acquire/release. `--barrier paranoid` also inserts a full hardware fence (mfence / dmb ish / fence rw,rw / __sync_synchronize) at every boundary.
constraints: volatile alone does not order accesses between CPUs (the runtime uses atomic instructions with explicit ordering).

name: CAS singly linked list
summary: Path for returning chunks from other CPUs (lock-free)
detail: When a chunk belongs to another CPU, it is pushed onto the head of that CPU's remote-free list with CAS (Release). The owning CPU takes the whole list with swap(NULL, Acquire), so the ABA problem cannot occur. The list head has its own cache line, so there is no split lock (a bus lock caused by a LOCK instruction spanning lines).

name: Deferred reclamation
summary: Frees from an ISR are reclaimed when normal context resumes
detail: Frees from an ISR are queued in CPU-local SPSC rings, one per nesting depth. Synchronizing with interrupts on the same CPU needs only compiler barriers, so the interrupt path never uses LOCK-prefixed instructions or hardware fences (interrupt latency does not get worse). Reclamation happens at safe points in normal context (fascon_rt_poll / region_cleanup).
constraints: A full ring is FASCON_PANIC_DEFER_FULL.

name: Isr pool placement
summary: Pinning the Isr region to TCM / scratchpad / cache-locked addresses
detail: `fascon gen-ld --board <name>` generates a linker script for each board and places the .fascon_isr section in very fast per-CPU SRAM (Cortex-M7 DTCM, Cortex-R5 BTCM [core-local alias], SiFive U74 L2 LIM, etc.). On x86_64 / QEMU without TCM it goes into normal RAM and is pre-faulted and warmed up at boot (staying resident in L1 cannot be guaranteed by the hardware).
constraints: x86 has no L1 cache lock. Many ARMv8-A cores do not support L1 lockdown either.

name: Page pinning
summary: Pinning every memory pool to physical memory at boot (identity map)
detail: The boot code of mas-runtime identity-maps (virtual = physical) all the pools of the five region classes and maps them in advance with large pages that have the present bit set (AArch64: 1 GiB/2 MiB blocks, x86_64: 2 MiB pages). There is no demand paging, so page faults cannot happen. A TLB miss is resolved by the hardware page walk and is not an exception (large pages also minimize TLB misses). Every pool is also written at boot (pre-faulting).
constraints: On AArch64 with the MMU off, every data access is treated as Device-nGnRnE, so exclusive loads/stores (CAS) and caches do not work correctly; the runtime therefore rejects the MMU-off configuration. RISC-V works safely with satp=Bare (MMU off). x86_64 long mode requires paging, so the identity map is used.
aliases: アイデンティティマッピング

name: ROM boot
summary: Keeping initialized data in flash and copying it to RAM right after reset (LMA / VMA)
detail: On microcontrollers that boot from flash (stm32h743-cm7 / qemu-mps2-an500), the linker script from `fascon gen-ld` places the initial values of .fascon_kernel (statics) and .data in flash (LMA) and their run-time addresses in RAM (VMA). CPU0 calls fascon_board_init_sections() from <board>_board.h in its first C function to copy flash to RAM and zero .bss. The Cortex-M vector table is placed at the start of flash (initial SP, reset handler); Cortex-R5 has no VBAR, so it is placed at 0x0 in ATCM (both are checked with ASSERT at link time). PHDRS splits the segments into R+X (code) and R+W (data), and no RWX segment is created.
constraints: Do not use .data / .bss / statics until the copy is complete (and keep interrupts disabled).

name: fascon_plat_kernel_panic
summary: Safe-stop hook (complete memory exhaustion, etc.)
detail: Always called on complete memory exhaustion (0x0001), Isr capacity overflow (0x0900), integer overflow (0x000B) and so on, and never returns. Implemented by the BSP.

name: O(1) bump allocation
summary: Lock-free, CPU-local fast path
detail: An allocation only advances the bump pointer (inlined). The next cache line is prefetched with write intent. Chunks come from a CPU-local pre-allocated pool; when it is empty, it is refilled from the list returned by other CPUs, then from the global reserve (spin lock), and exhaustion is a panic.

name: fascon build
summary: Generate C code (build/<name>.fascon.c)
detail: The source file is never overwritten, even when the input is a .c file. fascon_rt.h is written next to it.
remedy: `fascon build main.rs --cache-line 64 --barrier strict`

name: fascon explain
summary: Root-cause timeline, fixed code and mathematical explanation
remedy: `fascon explain main.rs --line 15`

name: fascon gen-ld
summary: Generate a linker script for a board
detail: Writes the linker script (.ld) and <board>_board.h (constants, fascon_board_init_sections()) and prints the C compiler flags required for that board (e.g. -mno-red-zone on x86_64, -mno-outline-atomics on AArch64).
remedy: `fascon gen-ld --list` / `fascon gen-ld --board stm32h743-cm7`

name: fascon lsp
summary: Language server (usable from editors other than VS Code)
detail: Start `fascon lsp` from the LSP client of Neovim / Emacs / Sublime Text / Helix / JetBrains.

name: arena
summary: a type-safe static region `arena name: T[N];` (the `@` is optional)
detail: Places a table of capacity N (1 to 16,777,216) in the Kernel region (.bss). Elements are inline values (in 16-byte-aligned slots) and each slot has a 32-bit generation tag. The compiler picks the index width K = ceil(log2(N)); the remaining 32-K bits are the generation (16 | 16 for a capacity of 65,536). The table holds 2^K slots + 1 sentinel. A slot is reused up to 2^(32-K)-1 times and then retires (generations never wrap), so an arena serves roughly 2.1 to 4.3 billion allocations over its life. The building block for OS tables (processes, files ...) that link to each other through Ids instead of pointers.
constraints: Elements cannot be references or bare arrays (put arrays in a struct field); own T fields are allowed (freed with the slot). A power-of-two capacity leaves no padding slots.
remedy: Split even larger tables into several arenas (the index has at most 24 bits).

aliases: クロス・インデックス型
constraints: An Id cannot be made from an integer (validate external values).
detail: `Id<@file>` and `Id<@process>` are different types (mixing them is F2101). Ids are copyable values, so they can be stored anywhere and express cyclic graphs (parent/child/sibling/back links) without references. `Option<Id<@a>>` uses 0 as None and stays 4 bytes.
name: Id<@a>
remedy: Inspect it with `.index()` / `.generation()` / `.raw()`.
summary: a handle coloured by its arena (32 bits: generation 32-K + index K, with K set by the capacity)

name: 世代タグ
summary: the reuse counter that prevents the ABA problem
detail: Freeing a slot increments its generation; an old Id no longer matches, so even if the slot was reused it yields None (or a safe stop for @a[id]). The check is one index-range compare plus one generation compare.
constraints: A slot has 65535 generations; an exhausted slot is retired and never handed out again (ABA is excluded structurally, not probabilistically).
remedy: Give long-running kernels some spare capacity (FIFO reuse spreads wear over all slots).

constraints: While the reference is live, functions that touch (free) slots of the same arena cannot be called: F2502; effects are computed transitively through callees.
detail: `if let Some(p) = @process.get_mut(pid) { p.state = 1; }`. p is a second-class reference that cannot leave the block; a stale Id takes the None arm.
name: @a.get / @a.get_mut
remedy: Copy what you need into locals, leave the block, then do the operation.
summary: a temporary lookup (a reference that exists only inside if let / match)

constraints: Passing two &mut of the same arena to one call is F0499 (the Ids may be equal).
detail: Used to read/write fields and to pass `&mut @a[id]`. Where liveness is statically proven (right after alloc, inside a successful lookup, after an earlier check) the generation check is omitted (see the counts with `fascon regions`).
name: @a[id]
remedy: Copy one side into a local, or split the call.
summary: a checked slot access (a stale Id stops safely)

constraints: Reuse is FIFO (in freeing order).
detail: alloc(v) → Option<Id> (None when full). free(id) → bool (also frees own fields; generation +1). remove(id) → Option<T> (moves the value out). validate(raw: u32) → Option<Id> (turns a value from outside, e.g. a syscall, back into an Id safely). `for id in @a { }` visits live slots only (the body may free).
name: @a.alloc / free / remove / validate
summary: allocate, free, take out, and validate external values

name: own T
summary: a move-only owning reference (exactly one owner in the world)
detail: `own Window { .. }` creates one own region. It cannot be copied or shared, only moved. Scope end, overwrite, `drop(x)` or an arena free releases it together with all descendants. It can be lent to functions as `&w`. The contents need not be a struct: `struct MyContext { buffer: own i32, size: i32 }` / `own [u8; 4096]` / `own Str` / `own Option<own Node>`. The contents of a non-struct own are read and written with `*` (`*ctx.buffer += 1;`). A struct with own fields is move-only too: every move, scope end and overwrite frees the owns inside along with it (double frees cannot happen, statically: F0382 / F0507).
constraints: The contents of an own are a value type (a struct, an integer, bool, Str, an Id, an array or an Option); references, `()`, `own own T` and function pointers are rejected (F0515 / F2301). A child cannot be moved out of an own field (F0507), nor a non-copyable value out of `*b` (F0507).
remedy: Use `Option<own T>` and `.take()` for detachable children. Replace the whole own with `ctx.buffer = own 7;`; write only its contents with `*ctx.buffer = 7;`.

name: 所有リージョン
summary: the box an own value lives in; children of the construction are packed into it
detail: `own Window { ok: own Button {..}, cancel: own Button {..} }` packs the window and its two buttons into one block with a single allocation (contiguous in cache). Closing it frees everything with a single free. Children replaced later get their own boxes and are freed immediately on replacement.
constraints: The contents of Option<own T> are never packed (they are detachable). One box is at most 64 KiB.
remedy: `fascon regions` shows how many children were packed.

name: .take() / drop()
summary: move out of an Option / free right now
detail: `desk.win.take()` returns the contents and leaves None. `drop(x)` frees the own region of x on the spot.
constraints: take needs a writable place (a mut variable, a &mut parameter, a slot).

name: mmio
summary: a fixed-address region `mmio @name: [T; N] at address;`
detail: Declares a physical address range as a typed array (1-D or 2-D). Indices proven in range are unchecked, constant out-of-range indices are compile-time errors (F2201), others are checked at run time. Devices default to volatile + I/O barriers (the ordering of Linux readl / writel).
constraints: Elements are u8 to u64. Two overlapping regions are F2203. References (&@fb[..]) cannot be created.
remedy: No raw pointers or unsafe are needed; volatile_bypass remains for compatibility.

name: #[framebuffer]
summary: a framebuffer treated as normal memory
detail: No volatile is applied, so full-screen loops are vectorized by GCC / Clang (e.g. NEON; the same machine code as raw pointers). The BSP reads the generated MMIO table, configures the ramfb of QEMU and maps the pages non-cacheable.
constraints: Pixels are 32 bits (XRGB8888).
remedy: `@fb.fill_rect(x, y, w, h, c)` and `@fb.put(x, y, c)` clip everything off-screen.

name: Str
summary: string literals (immutable strings in the Kernel region)
detail: Can be stored anywhere (it lives forever). `.len()`, `.byte(i)`, `==`.
constraints: Strings cannot be built at run time.

name: [T; N]
summary: fixed-size arrays (inline values)
detail: `[None; 16]`, `[1, 2, 3]`. Indexing is checked, and omitted where the range is proven (e.g. inside `for i in 0..N`).
constraints: Not passable or returnable by value (F2040): pass `&[T; N]`.

name: type 別名<@a: T>
summary: type aliases with arena parameters and kind bounds
detail: `type FileId<@a: File> = Id<@a>;` → `FileId<@file>`. The bound `@a: File` only admits arenas whose element type is File (violations are F2102).

name: if let
summary: a match that tries a single pattern
detail: Used on a place (a variable or field) the binding is a reference (a borrow); used on a value (a call result, take()) it receives ownership.

name: 生存ビットマップ
summary: a liveness table with one bit per slot (64 slots = one uint64_t)
detail: alloc sets the bit and free / remove clears it. A general `for id in @a` reads one word and finds the next live slot with ctz (x86-64: TZCNT / AArch64: RBIT + CLZ), so there is no per-slot branch and no read of a live mark. Filtered counts and min / max exclude dead slots with a mask made of the live bit of each slot ANDed with the filter. A word that is all zero skips 64 slots without reading them.
constraints: 8 KiB for 65,536 slots; the array starts on its own 128-byte boundary, apart from the other arrays (SoA).
remedy: `fascon regions` shows how many loops run on the bitmap and how many reductions are masked.

name: 列
summary: dense mirrors inside the table holding exactly the values a `for id in @a` reduction reads (aggregate, bit and key columns)
detail: The compiler looks at every `for id in @a` reduction in the program and gives each one columns in the table (no annotation in the source). Sums and filtered sums → aggregate column agg[i] = filter ? value : 0 (8 B per slot for u64 values, 4 B for 32 bits or fewer). Filtered counts → bit column (bit i = live && filter; the count is one popcount per 64 slots). Min / max picks → key column key[i] = live && filter ? enc(value) : NONE (the scan is a signed minimum). Scans read the columns, never the slots, so even a 32-byte task costs 1 bit to 8 bytes of traffic. Columns mirror the slots: alloc, free / remove, writes by Id that reach a field a column reads, the end of a get_mut borrow, and calls given &mut @a[id] rebuild exactly the columns the write can reach. During a borrow F2502 rejects every read of the arena, so a stale mirror is never observed.
constraints: Each column adds 4 to 8 B × 2^K to the table (a bit column 2^K bits); `fascon regions` lists them with the total. Reductions whose filter reads a local (a parameter, say) and 64-bit `<=` / `>=` picks get no column and keep the 1.0.0 scan. A write costs one store per column it reaches (writes to fields no column reads cost nothing extra).
remedy: `--columns off` (VS Code: setting fascon.columns; environment FASCON_COLUMNS=off) gives back the 1.0.0 tables and scans.

name: #[repr(align(N))]
summary: raises the alignment of a struct to at least N bytes (N a power of two from 1 to 4096)
detail: As an arena element, every slot gets an N-byte boundary: N = 64 puts one slot per line and N = 128 also separates it from the adjacent line, so slots written by different cores never share a line. The table itself (bookkeeping, live bitmap, generations, links, slots) is split on 128-byte boundaries even without it.
constraints: A type aligned to more than 16 bytes cannot live in an own region (16-byte aligned; F2032). On small slots it makes the table larger and scans read more bytes.
remedy: Use it only on tables that each core writes; keep scan-heavy tables at 16 bytes.

name: フレームリージョン
summary: where an own that is never moved lives, with the same motion as a stack
detail: A `let x = own T { .. }` that escape analysis shows is never moved is taken from a pre-reserved frame by bumping its top pointer (one compare and one add, inlined) instead of the heap free lists, and popped back to its mark where the scope of x ends (break, continue and return included). Inside a loop it is popped every iteration, so it does not grow. The MMU and page tables are never touched.
constraints: An own that is returned, stored in a struct or arena, passed by value or dropped stays on the heap. When the frame is full, allocation falls back to the heap (same result). The BSP frame is 1 MiB; PC runs default to 64 KiB.
remedy: The "frame region" lines of `fascon regions` show which lets were placed in the frame.

name: own_alloc(T)
summary: dynamic allocation taking a type name (no generics): a zero-filled own T
detail: `let data = own_alloc(Block);` returns a zero-filled `own Block`. Its own children (non-Option own fields, also inside arrays and inline structs) are created zero-filled and packed into the same own region (one allocation, one free); Option<own T> fields start as None. A let that is never moved takes it from the frame region. It is freed automatically at the end of its scope.
constraints: The argument is a value type an own can hold (a struct, an integer, bool, Str, an Id, an array or an Option; `own_alloc(i32)` / `own_alloc([u8; 4096])` work too; anything else is F2301); types whose own children never end are rejected (F2304: make the way back Option<own T>); no alignment above 16 bytes (F2032).

name: コミット点
summary: where the latch (deferred faults) is checked and the program stops safely
detail: Placed right before calls, output, MMIO and exit, and before return. Loops with a fixed trip count (`for i in a..b`, `for id in @a`) carry none inside and check once at the exit (one jump fewer in the body, and a shape that can be vectorized). In loops without a fixed trip count (while, loop) the latch is folded into the exit condition and shares the branch of the exit.
constraints: After a stale read, a fixed-trip loop runs to its last iteration before stopping (anything with an external effect stops first).
remedy: Where it stopped is the source position written in the `F20_COMMIT`.

name: F2101
summary: arena colour mismatch
detail: An Id of one arena was used to index or fill a field of another arena.
constraints: Id<@a> and Id<@b> (a ≠ b) are different types.
remedy: Use an Id obtained from the right arena; validate external values.

name: F2102
summary: kind bound violated
detail: An arena that does not store File was given to `FileId<@a: File>`.
remedy: Pass an arena that matches the bound.

name: F2103
summary: invalid arena declaration (capacity 1..16,777,216, value elements other than bare arrays; bump_arena elements cannot hold own)
detail: An arena declaration has the wrong shape: a capacity outside 1 to 16,777,216 (the index of an Id has at most 24 bits), an element that is not a value type (`own T`, an array or a function pointer cannot be the element directly), or a bump_arena element that contains own (the bulk release of a call region does not run own releases).
remedy: Keep the capacity inside the range. Put own, arrays and function pointers inside struct fields and make that struct the element. Keep values that hold own in an `arena`, not a bump_arena.

name: F2104
summary: an arena or region name that is declared nowhere (declaration order is free: declaring it later is fine)
detail: An arena name used in `@name`, `Id<@name>`, `for task` and the like cannot be found, or the name of an MMIO region or a port was given to `Id` (an `Id` only refers to arenas). Declarations may come in any order, so declaring it later is fine.
remedy: Match the spelling to the declaration, or declare `arena name: Type[N];`.

name: F2201
summary: fixed-address region index out of bounds (compile time)
detail: A fixed-address region (mmio, #[framebuffer], ...) is accessed with an index known at compile time that lies outside it. Writing past it would damage other devices or memory, so the compiler stops it (F0608 for ordinary arrays).
remedy: Fix the index, or use the clipping put / fill_rect.

name: F2202
summary: invalid MMIO declaration (type, alignment, address)
detail: The form `mmio name: [u32; N] at address;` is wrong: the type is not an array of integers (one or two dimensions, u8 to u64 elements), the address is not aligned to the element size, the range does not fit the address space, or the address is 0.
remedy: Follow the addresses and register widths of the data sheet and write `[u32; N]` or `[[u32; W]; H]`.

name: F2203
summary: overlapping MMIO regions
detail: Two MMIO regions (or two ports) have overlapping address ranges. If the same physical memory or register could be written under two names, the checks would mean nothing.
remedy: Separate the ranges, or merge them into one region and tell the parts apart by index.

name: F2204
summary: a region used as a value or a reference
detail: `@a` itself is not a value, nor is a row `@fb[y]`.
remedy: Use `@a[id]`, `@a.alloc(..)`, `@fb[y][x]`.

name: F2301
summary: own applied to a type an own cannot hold (`()`, `own own T`, a function pointer)
detail: The contents of an own are a value type (a struct, an integer, bool, Str, an Id, an array or an Option). `own own T` needs only one level, and a function pointer holds no data, so keep it as a plain value. Putting a reference into an own is F0515 (F0520 inside a callback).
remedy: Use `own T`, or a plain value.

name: F2302
summary: a static holding a type that contains own
detail: A static holds a type that contains own. Statics live in the Kernel region and are immutable, so the own could never be released.
remedy: Keep values that hold own in an arena, and keep integers or Ids in statics.

name: F2502
summary: arena effect conflict (touching an arena while a reference into it is live)
detail: While a lookup or &mut @a[id] reference was live, a function that reads/writes/frees slots of that arena (including through callees) was called, or the arena was touched directly. A call through a function pointer (a callback) is checked against the union of the effects of every function that can be passed there, and the conflicting one is named (e.g. a function that frees tasks passed as f in `for id in tasks { f(&mut tasks[id]); }`).
constraints: Effects are computed as a least fixpoint over the call graph (function-pointer candidates included).
remedy: Copy values into locals and call outside the block.

name: F2900
summary: a 0.1-only feature (spawn / chan / async / #[isr]) in a file using 1.0 syntax
detail: This release has two engines: files with 1.0 syntax (arena / own / mmio) go to the 1.0 engine, others to the 0.1 core.
remedy: Put the threaded / interrupt parts in a separate file (0.1 core).

name: F2030
summary: an infinitely sized struct (contains itself by value)
detail: In 1.0 structs are inline values.
remedy: Recurse through `Option<own T>`.

name: F2031
summary: a malformed `#[repr(align(N))]` or an invalid N
detail: The only supported repr is `#[repr(align(N))]` with N a power of two from 1 to 4096; other attributes on a struct are ignored (warning).
remedy: Write it like `#[repr(align(64))]` or `#[repr(align(128))]`.

name: F2032
summary: a type aligned to more than 16 bytes was put in an own region
detail: Own regions (and frame regions) are 16-byte aligned, so a `#[repr(align(64))]` struct, or a type that contains one by value, would lose its alignment there.
remedy: Use it as an arena element or as a plain value (a local or a struct field).

name: F2040
summary: arrays passed or returned by value
detail: An array is passed by value, returned, or has length 0. This avoids hidden copies of large arrays.
remedy: Pass `&[T; N]`, or return the array inside a struct.

name: fn(T) -> R
summary: a function pointer (callback) type; using the name of a function as a value makes one
detail: Write `fn for_each(a: &mut [i32; 4], f: fn(&mut i32)) { for i in 0..4 { f(&mut a[i]); } }` and pass the name of a function, as in `for_each(&mut a, inc)`. Its parameters are parameter positions, so reference types `&T` / `&mut T` are allowed (still second-class: alive for the call only). It can live in struct fields (`on_click: fn(&mut Button)`), locals, static tables (`static OPS: [fn(i32) -> i32; 2] = [inc, dbl];`) and `Option<fn(..)>`. A function pointer in a field is called as `(h.on_click)(&mut b)`. In C it is a function pointer type made with typedef (`fsc_fnN`); it holds no data (it is copyable).
constraints: The return type cannot be a reference (F0515); arrays cannot be passed or returned by value (F2040); types must agree in every parameter type, reference mutability and the return type (F0308). Callbacks that receive references must be stack_only (F0520). The effect of a call is the union over every function that can be passed (F2502). `main` and builtins cannot be values.
remedy: To give a callback state, pass the state along as a `&mut` parameter (there are no closures).

name: stack_only
summary: the property that a callback consumes the references it receives inside its own stack frame (guaranteed by F0520)
detail: Using a function with reference parameters as a value (making it a callback) requires it to be stack_only: it may read and write through the references and pass them on as reference arguments, but must not put them into an arena, a static, MMIO, the places of the caller (behind another reference), an own region or a by-value parameter, nor return them. References made from references (`&mut x.f`, bindings of places), values wrapping a reference (`Some(x)`, structs, arrays) and locals bound to one are followed, and so are paths through callees, by per-function summaries (a least fixpoint over the call graph).
constraints: Thanks to second-class references (F0515), a program that type-checks is stack_only already; F0520 points out code that departs from it, in the context of the callback and with a root-cause timeline (folding F0515 / F0308 at the same places).
remedy: To keep the data, copy the contents (`*x` / `x.clone()`) or hold the target by `Id` or `own`.

name: F0520
summary: reference escape constraint violated: a callback let a reference it received escape
detail: A callback assigned or stored a second-class reference that a higher-order function lent it for one call (`f(&mut a[i])`) into something that outlives the call (an arena, a static, MMIO, the places of the caller, an own, a by-value parameter), or returned it. The timeline reads: which higher-order function it was passed to → which reference parameter → wrapping / binding / passing to another function → where it escapes.
constraints: Callback = a function with reference parameters that is used as a value.
remedy: Copy the contents (`*x` / `x.clone()`) or hold the target by `Id` / `own`. `fascon explain <file> --code F0520` shows the path and the fix.

name: F0560
summary: A struct literal names a field the struct does not have
detail: A struct literal `S { .. }` gives a field that the declaration does not have.
remedy: Match the field names to the declaration.

name: F0618
summary: called something that is not a function
detail: The x of `x(1)` is neither a function nor a function pointer `fn(..)`.
remedy: Call a function pointer stored in a field with parentheses: `(h.cb)(..)`.

name: fascon qemu
summary: build and run on QEMU (BIOS-less AArch64, or x86_64 / AArch64 through the Fascon virtual BIOS; GUI capable)
detail: `fascon qemu app.fsc` → generate C, write the BSP, link with clang / gcc, start QEMU (AArch64, -kernel). `--target x86_64` / `--target aarch64` boots through the Fascon virtual BIOS (-bios). Programs that use `spawn_on` boot with `-smp 4` (`--smp N` for 1 to 4). `--headless --screenshot out.png` saves the screen.
constraints: Needs clang + ld.lld (or aarch64 / x86_64 gcc) and qemu-system-aarch64 (qemu-system-x86_64 for `--target x86_64`).

name: fascon run
summary: build and run on the PC (the framebuffer is saved as PNG)
detail: Maps the fixed-address regions at the same addresses inside the process. A GUI is written to `<name>.png` at exit. The generated C is compiled for the CPU of this PC (x86-64: -march=native, AArch64: -mcpu=native, so column scans use AVX2 / AVX-512 / NEON widths; a compiler that rejects the flag gets a second try without it). `--cpu baseline` sticks to the baseline instructions of the architecture.

name: critical
summary: A closed section (a block or function that is not interrupted)
detail: Inside `critical { .. }` and `critical fn` neither interrupts nor task switches happen. On multi-core it (1) masks the interrupts of this core and (2) takes the spinlock, and releases them in reverse order on exit (`fascon_plat_critical_enter` / `exit`; DAIF.I on AArch64, RFLAGS.IF on x86_64). The compiler finds which regions are shared from the effects, so nothing is written on the regions.
constraints: The end of a closed section is a commit point. `@task.yield_to` may be called inside (the interrupt state lives in the saved frame). On multi-core, waiting inside (channel send / recv_wait, task waits) is F2603, and gc_arena allocation and collection are F2622.
remedy: The Quick Fix of F2601 wraps the statements in `critical { .. }`.
aliases: クリティカルセクション

name: task_arena
summary: The task table arena
detail: `task_arena @task: Task[64] stack 16384;` is an arena whose slots also carry a kernel stack and a saved context (hidden columns). `@task.start(value, entry, arg)`, `current()`, `yield_to(id)`, `resume(id)` (irq only), `enter(id)`, `exit()`. The policy (choosing the next task) is written in Fascon.
constraints: The entry is a `fn(u64)`. The current task cannot be freed (F2605). In a program that uses `spawn_on` there is one task table per core (slot i is a different task on each core).
aliases: コンテキストスイッチ

name: #[wire(le)] / #[wire(be)]
summary: Wire structs (alignment 1, no padding, fixed byte order, plain old data)
detail: Fields are integers, arrays of integers and wire structs only. Every bit pattern is a valid value, so they can be laid over disk sectors, packets, memory shared with a device and user memory.
constraints: A layout that would need padding is F2701 (reorder the fields or write a reserved field).

name: .view(T, off) / .window(off, len)
summary: Views and windows over bytes (second-class references)
detail: `x.view(T, off)` is a reference to a wire struct over bytes; `x.window(off, len)` is a reference with a length, `&[u8]`. Both give None when out of range and never stop. `x.read(T, off)` copies. Being references they cannot be stored (F0515).
constraints: Only as the scrutinee of `if let` / `match`. `&a[lo..hi]` panics when out of range, so use it for trusted values only.

name: dma / dma_arena / Dma<@b>
summary: Memory shared with devices, and lending expressed as a move
detail: `dma @r: [T; N];` is a ring both sides touch (always volatile). `dma_arena @b: T[N];` is a table of buffers and `Dma<@b>` its move-only handle. `@b.lend(h)` consumes h (later use is F0382); `@b.reclaim(index)` returns a handle only if the index is in range and lent.
constraints: Elements are plain old data (F2702). Handles cannot live in a bump_arena or a static (F2703).
remedy: Take the address as an integer with `h.phys()` / `@r.phys()` and write it into the descriptor.

name: syscall / user_mem / trap
summary: The boundary with user space (EL0 on AArch64, ring 3 on x86_64)
detail: `user_mem umem for task: 0x8_0000 at 0x1_0000_0000;` is per-task user memory (size and address are multiples of 4 KiB; every task sees the same virtual address). Every task has its own page table (address space), and pages are mapped 4 KiB at a time when first touched (demand paging). `task.start_user(value, entry, stack)` creates a user task and `if let Some(m) = umem.of(id) { .. }` lets the kernel write its image. `syscall write at 1 (fd: u32, buf: &[u8]) -> i64 { .. }` is an entry from user space: windows and references to wire structs reach the body only after the entry has checked that they lie inside the user memory of the calling task (otherwise the body is not entered and the result is -14; a `&mut` window overlapping another window is -14 too). On multi-core the entry copies each window once into a shadow buffer, so another core changing the memory meanwhile cannot change what the body sees (`&mut` windows are written back on exit). A bodiless `syscall .. -> i64;` is the user-side declaration and becomes an svc (`int $0x80` on x86_64). `trap user_fault(esr: u64, far: u64, pc: u64) { .. }` runs on user exceptions; when it returns only that task ends (x86_64 exceptions are translated into the classes of the AArch64 ESR; far is CR2 and pc is RIP).
constraints: Ids, own, Dma, Str, bool and function pointers cannot be parameters (F2801). Numbers are 0 to 255 and distinct (F2802).
remedy: Take an Id as a u32 and pass it through `@a.validate(raw)`.

name: F2601
summary: Unprotected access to a shared region
detail: In an open section (interrupts enabled) the code touches a region that another execution root (an irq handler or another task) writes, frees or allocates in.On multi-core, an irq body only masks the interrupts of its own core while other cores keep running, so shared instances (shared arena and the like) need critical (the lock); the effects of every root on other cores (task, syscall, irq) are part of the environment effect E_env (per-core arenas excluded).
remedy: Wrap the statements in `critical { .. }` (Quick Fix) or make the function a `critical fn`.

name: F2603
summary: A task switch in interrupt context, or resume outside an interrupt
detail: A function reachable from an irq handler calls something that may switch (`yield_to`, `exit`), or `@task.resume` is called outside an irq.On multi-core, blocking operations inside critical (channel send / recv_wait, task switches and waits) are rejected with this code too (sleeping while holding the lock would stop the other cores).
remedy: Use `resume` inside an irq and `yield_to` inside a task.

name: F2701 / F2702 / F2703
summary: Wire struct layout / non-POD DMA element / where a Dma handle may live
detail: F2701: a wire struct would need padding or has a field that is not an integer, an array of integers or a wire struct. F2702: an element of `dma` / `dma_arena` contains bool, Option, an Id, own, Str or a function pointer. F2703: a `Dma<@b>` is stored in a bump_arena, a static or another table.
remedy: F2701: add `#[wire(le)]` or `#[wire(be)]` and use only integers, integer arrays and wire structs as fields. F2702: keep DMA elements to integers and integer arrays (wire structs), and keep Ids and own in ordinary arenas. F2703: use the handles returned by `alloc` and `reclaim`, keep them in locals or in an ordinary arena or array (do not iterate the dma_arena itself), and validate an index returned by the device with `reclaim(raw)`.

name: F2704
summary: An untrusted value reaches an operation that can stop the kernel
detail: An integer that came from a device, user memory, the wire or a system call argument is used directly in checked arithmetic, a stopping index or `unwrap`; the kernel could be stopped from outside. Design stage: not accepted by the bundled 1.0 compiler yet (docs/SPEC-1.0-KERNEL.ja.md, Japanese).
remedy: Pass it through `checked_add`, `wrapping_add`, `min` or `window` (none of which stop).

name: F2801 / F2802 / F2803
summary: The shape of a system call / numbers and registers / where things cannot be used
detail: F2801: a system call parameter that is not an integer, `&[u8]` / `&mut [u8]` or a reference to a wire struct (take an Id as `u32` and pass it through `validate`), a result that is not `i64`, a wrong `trap` shape, or a syscall / trap called from inside the kernel. F2802: a number outside 0..=255 or used twice, or parameters taking more than 8 registers (a window takes 2). F2803: a kernel item in a user program (EL0), a `user_mem` size or address that is not a multiple of 4 KiB, lies inside the identity map (0 to 0x8000_0000), reaches 0x80_0000_0000 or crosses a 1 GiB slot (on the x86_64 virtual BIOS the BSP also requires 4 GiB or more at boot), `start_user` on a task_arena without `user_mem`, or an unreadable ABI source.
remedy: F2801: take an Id as `u32` and `validate` it in the body, pass bytes as windows `&[u8]` / `&mut [u8]`, and return `i64`. F2802: use a free number from 0 to 255 and keep the parameters within 8 registers (a window takes 2). F2803: put kernel items in the kernel file; make the size and address of `user_mem` multiples of 4 KiB, outside the identity map, below 0x80_0000_0000 and inside one 1 GiB slot.

name: F2804
summary: An embed error
detail: The file of `static NAME: [u8; N] = embed("file name");` cannot be read or is larger than N bytes, or `embed` is used in another form. A relative path is taken from the folder of the source file.
remedy: Check where the file is, and make N at least the file size (the size the message suggests is fine).

name: F2602 / F2605
summary: The shape of an interrupt handler / of a task_arena
detail: F2602: an INTID outside 16..=1019, two handlers for one INTID, or an interrupt handler called as a function. F2605: a task_arena stack that is not a multiple of 16 from 4096 to 1048576, a capacity above 256, two task_arenas, or a task entry that is not a `fn(u64)`.
remedy: F2602: use distinct INTIDs from 16 to 1019 and let interrupts run the handlers instead of calling them (put shared work in another function and call that from both). F2605: make the stack a multiple of 16 from 4096 to 1048576 and the capacity at most 256, keep a single task_arena, and make the entry a `fn(u64)`.

name: timer_arm / irq_open / wait_irq
summary: Builtins for the timer and for enabling interrupts
detail: `timer_freq()` (Hz), `timer_now()` (the counter), `timer_arm(ticks)` (a timer interrupt after `ticks`), `irq_open()` (enable interrupts; in main everything before it is the boot context) and `wait_irq()` (wait for an interrupt without losing one that arrives between the check and the wait). The clock is shared by all cores and the timer is per core. On AArch64 this is the virtual timer (INTID 27); on the x86_64 virtual BIOS the clock is the HPET and the timer is the LAPIC timer (the same irq 27). On a PC it is a virtual clock, and `cpu_relax()`, `wait_irq()` and the end of a closed section are the points where interrupts arrive.
constraints: A user function of the same name takes precedence.

name: put_bytes / embed
summary: Write a window to the console / embed a file in a static
detail: `put_bytes(buf)` writes the bytes of a window (`&[u8]`, `&[u8; N]` or a string) as they are. `static IMG: [u8; N] = embed("file.bin");` embeds the bytes of a file (zero-padded; relative paths start at the folder of the source file). Used to put a user program image into the kernel.
constraints: F2804: the file cannot be read, does not fit in the array, or the form is not `static NAME: [u8; N] = embed("..")`.
remedy: Build the image with `fascon build app.fsc --out app.bin`.

name: // fascon-abi: kernel.fsc
summary: This file is a user program (EL0)
detail: The comment `// fascon-abi: kernel.fsc` near the top of a file imports the `syscall` declarations and wire structs of that kernel source (the same as `fascon build --user app.fsc --abi kernel.fsc`). `fascon build app.fsc --out app.bin` makes a flat image linked at the address of the `user_mem` of the kernel. Printing goes to fd 1 of the `write(fd: u32, buf: &[u8])` of the ABI; the end of main and panics (exit code 70) go to `exit(code)`.
constraints: F2803: a user program cannot use mmio, port_io, irq, critical, dma, task_arena, user_mem, trap, a syscall with a body, shared arena, chan or spawn_on.

name: shared arena
summary: An arena with one instance for every core (the SMP extension of Fascon 1.0)
detail: `shared arena procs: Proc[64];`. In a program that uses `spawn_on` a plain `arena` has one instance per core and is accessed by the single-core code (no locks). A shared arena is touched only inside `critical { }` (a writer) or `for id in procs.par()` (a reader); outside it is F2601. Its Ids may cross cores.
constraints: F2611: the elements of a shared arena cannot hold Ids of per-core arenas.
remedy: Specification: docs/SPEC-1.0-SMP.ja.md (Japanese)

name: spawn_on / cpu_count
summary: Run a function on another core (the SMP extension of Fascon 1.0)
detail: `spawn_on(1, worker);` / `spawn_on(2, worker, arg);`. The function takes 0 or 1 parameter and returns nothing; the argument is an integer, a bool, an Id of a shared arena or an `own T` (which moves). `cpu_count()` is the number of usable cores. `fascon qemu` boots with `-smp 4` (`--smp N` for 1 to 4); on the PC a core is a thread. A missing or busy core is panic 0x0012.
constraints: F2615: a wrong function shape or argument type. The former F2614 (which rejected `spawn_on` together with irq, task_arena, dma_arena, syscall and trap) is retired: the task table, the current task, the run queue and the timer are per core. The x86_64 virtual BIOS (`--target x86_64`) runs 4 cores too (the AArch64 virtual BIOS stays single-core because it has no PSCI).
remedy: A user function of the same name takes precedence.

name: for id in a.par()
summary: A read-only parallel scan of a shared arena (the SMP extension of Fascon 1.0)
detail: A scan that enters as a reader: it runs alongside the `par()` scans of other cores while writers (`critical`) wait. It does not split one loop over the cores. Collect results in locals and write them inside `critical` after the loop.
constraints: F2612: the body writes, allocates or frees a shared arena, calls a function that does (decided from the effects E(f)), or contains `critical`. Not for per-core arenas.

name: F2611
summary: An Id of a per-core arena crosses between cores
detail: A channel element, a shared arena element or a `spawn_on` argument contains (inside structs and owns too) an Id of a plain arena. A plain arena has a separate instance on every core, so the Id would refer to a different table there.
remedy: Declare tables shared between cores as `shared arena`; send per-core data with its ownership inside an `own T`.

name: F2612 / F2613
summary: A write inside a parallel scan / an unprotected device access
detail: F2612: a `par()` body contains something that modifies a shared arena (a direct write, allocation or free, a call of a function whose effects do, or `critical`). F2613: MMIO, a port or `mmio_read` / `mmio_write` reachable from two or more core roots is outside `critical`.
remedy: F2612: collect the results in locals and write them inside `critical { .. }` after the loop. F2613: wrap the statement in `critical { .. }` or make the function a `critical fn`.

name: F2614 / F2615
summary: Items that cannot be combined with spawn_on / the shape of spawn_on and chan
detail: F2614 (retired): earlier versions rejected irq, task_arena, dma_arena, syscall and trap in programs that use `spawn_on`; they now work together through per-core task tables, per-core timers and per-task address spaces (F2616, F2601, F2603 and F2613 reject the unsafe combinations instead). F2615: the second argument of `spawn_on` is not a function name, the argument count or type does not fit, a channel capacity is not a power of two (2 to 65536), or its element is neither `own T` nor a value that needs no drop.
remedy: F2615: the function of `spawn_on(core, function[, argument])` takes 0 or 1 parameter and returns nothing, and the argument is an integer, a bool, an Id of a shared arena or an `own T`. A channel capacity is a power of two from 2 to 65536 and its element is `own T` or a value that needs no drop. F2614 is retired, so combinations it used to reject can be written as they are.

name: F2616
summary: A shared-interrupt handler touches a per-core arena
detail: In a multi-core program the handler of a shared peripheral interrupt (INTID 32 and up, delivered to CPU0 only) touches a per-core arena (a plain arena, task_arena and other items with one instance per core); it would look up Ids made on other cores in the table of CPU0.
remedy: Make the arena a `shared arena` and touch it inside `critical { .. }`, or hand the data to the owning core through a `chan`. Handlers of per-core interrupts (16 to 31, such as the timer at INTID 27) may touch the instances of their own core.

name: fascon_plat_vm_*
summary: Per-task address spaces and switches without TLB flushes
detail: Every user task has its own page table (a 16-bit ASID and TTBR0 on AArch64, a PML4 and CR3 + PCID on x86_64). A switch only writes the table address and does not flush the TLB. Flushes happen only when a page is unmapped or a space is dropped, and only on the cores that used that ASID (other cores get an IPI / SGI shootdown; one sender at a time, and a waiting core keeps serving requests sent to it). Touching an unmapped page inside the user memory maps 4 KiB in the exception handler and retries the access (demand paging).
constraints: Pages are 4 KiB. QEMU TCG has no PCID, so the x86_64 PCID path was not executed in this environment (under TCG a CR3 write drops the non-global TLB entries).

name: copy_from_user / copy_to_user
summary: Shadow buffers that copy system-call windows exactly once (TOCTOU ruled out by construction)
detail: On multi-core, threads on other cores can change user memory at the same time. So the syscall entry copies each checked window once into a kernel shadow buffer with `fascon_plat_copy_from_user`, and the body reads only that copy (nothing is read twice, so nothing can be swapped between the check and the use). `&mut` windows are written back on exit by `fascon_plat_copy_to_user`. The copies run with user permissions (LDTRB / STTRB on AArch64, SMAP STAC / CLAC on x86_64), and failures become EFAULT (-14) through an exception table.
constraints: A shadow buffer holds up to 0xFFF0 bytes (longer windows give E2BIG = -7). Copies go one byte at a time and are not tuned for speed yet.

name: panic_broadcast / core_parked
summary: Stopping every core on a panic
detail: When a core panics, `fascon_plat_panic_broadcast` sends a stop interrupt to every other core (SGI 2 on AArch64, NMI on x86_64). Cores that notice the panic in a waiting loop stop in `fascon_plat_core_parked`; the stopped cores are counted and reported as "N other core(s) stopped" (exit code 70). An NMI also reaches masked sections, so even if a core stopped while holding the console lock, the panicking core takes the console over after a bounded wait and reports.

name: Id<a>
summary: a handle coloured by its arena (32 bits: generation 32-K + index K, with K set by the capacity)
detail: `Id<file>` and `Id<process>` are different types (mixing them is F2101). Ids are copyable values, so they can be stored anywhere and express cyclic graphs (parent/child/sibling/back links) without references. `Option<Id<a>>` uses 0 as None and stays 4 bytes. Ids of a bump_arena are 64 bits (generation 64-K | index K).
constraints: An Id cannot be made from an integer (validate external values).
remedy: Inspect it with `.index()` / `.generation()` / `.raw()`.
aliases: クロス・インデックス型

name: a.get / a.get_mut
summary: a temporary lookup (a reference that exists only inside if let / match)
