detail: `if let Some(p) = process.get_mut(pid) { p.state = 1; }`. p is a second-class reference that cannot leave the block; a stale Id takes the None arm. `process.get_mut(pid).unwrap().state = 1;` is the same expression as `process[pid].state = 1;` (the strict spelling; `.get(id).unwrap()` is read-only, and writing through it is F0596).
constraints: While the reference is live, functions that touch (free) slots of the same arena cannot be called: F2502; effects are computed transitively through callees.
remedy: Copy what you need into locals, leave the block, then do the operation.

name: a[id]
summary: a checked slot access (a stale Id stops safely); `pcb_table[id].id = 100;` is the generation-verified `.get_mut(id)`
detail: Used to read/write fields and to pass `&mut @a[id]`. Where liveness is statically proven (right after alloc, inside a successful lookup, after an earlier check) the generation check is omitted (see the counts with `fascon regions`).
constraints: Passing two &mut of the same arena to one call is F0499 (the Ids may be equal).
remedy: Copy one side into a local, or split the call.

name: a.alloc / free / remove / validate
summary: allocate, free, take out, and validate external values
detail: alloc(v) → Option<Id> (None when full). free(id) → bool (also frees own fields; generation +1). remove(id) → Option<T> (moves the value out). validate(raw: u32) → Option<Id> (turns a value from outside, e.g. a syscall, back into an Id safely). `for id in @a { }` visits live slots only (the body may free).
constraints: Reuse is FIFO (in freeing order).

name: bump_arena
summary: an arena released in bulk, in O(1), per call region `bump_arena name: T[N];`
detail: Allocation just advances the top (one compare + stores). At every exit of the allocating function (its call region) one store resets the top to the mark taken at entry, releasing everything at once. Ids are 64 bits [generation 64-K | index K]: every allocation of a slot bumps its generation, and the check is "index < top and the generation matches". After a rewind a stale Id yields None (or, for `b[id]`, a latch stopping at the next commit point), so it never reaches the data of anyone else. Allocations of functions that return Ids or pass them out through `&mut` parameters are promoted to the region of the caller. `for id in b` is a straight 0..top loop and `b.len()` is the current top.
constraints: No per-slot free / remove (F2401); elements cannot hold own (F2103); Ids cannot be stored in elements of long-lived tables (plain arenas, other bump arenas) or in statics (F2402).
remedy: Keep values freed one by one, and Ids stored for long, in an `arena`.
aliases: バンプアロケーション

name: port_io
summary: an x86 I/O port `port_io name[: u8 | u16 | u32 | [u8; N]] at_port number;`
detail: Reading it as a value is an in, assigning to it is an out (`com1 = c;` → x86_64 `out dx, al`, `let s = lsr;` → `in al, dx`). The type defaults to u8; array ports are indexed `p[i]` (bounds-checked). AArch64 has no I/O port space, so the compiler remaps to MMIO: COM1 (0x3f8-0x3ff) emulates a 16550 on the PL011 of QEMU virt (0x0900_0000: data → DR, LSR ← FR, the divisor while DLAB is set is only remembered), COM2-4 are not connected (LSR = 0x60), isa-debug-exit (0xf4 / 0x501) exits, and anything else goes to the PCI I/O window (0x3eff_0000 + port). `#[mmio_map(address)]` picks the target explicitly. PC runs emulate ports in the platform layer (COM1 transmit goes to stdout). `--target x86_64 / aarch64` emits only the form of that target. The strict form spells them `p.read()` / `p.write(v)` / `p.read_at(i)` / `p.write_at(i, v)`.
constraints: Elements are u8 / u16 / u32 and ports 0 to 0xFFFF (F2205); overlapping ports are F2203; no references (F2204).

name: put(x)
summary: a builtin printing an integer, a Str or a bool chosen by its type (no newline)
detail: With reframing, `println!("pid {} = {:#x}", a, b)` becomes `{ put_str("pid "); put(a); put_str(" = "); put_hex(b); print_str(""); }` (inline `{name}` captures work too).

name: 型推論
summary: lets need no type annotations (F0282 eradicated)
detail: The type of `let task = create_process(100);` comes from the return type; `let mut best = None;` and `let x;` are settled by later assignments, comparisons, calls and arena indexing (each function is type-checked twice, the first pass seeding the second). Integers and None that nothing uses default to i32. F0282 remains only when a still-unknown type is used as the base of a field, a method or an index.
remedy: If F0282 appears, write one type on that let (--emit-strict-fascon shows what was inferred).

name: @（省略可）
summary: region names need no `@` (and declarations may come in any order)
detail: Pass 1 registers every struct, arena, fn and port name; pass 2 reads the bodies. A bare name denotes the region unless a local of that name is in scope (`pcb_table[id]`). The old `@name` remains an explicit marker that always denotes the region (even under a local of the same name). Both give the same expression, so check elision and scan speed are unchanged.
constraints: Region names share the namespace of functions, statics and types (a clash is F0428).

name: 自動リフレーミング
summary: rewrites ordinary Rust syntax into Fascon forms before compiling (on / off)
detail: On with `#![reframing(rust)]` at the top or `--reframing=rust` (env FASCON_REFRAMING), off with `#![reframing(off)]` / `--reframing=off`. `#[link_section = ".uart"] static mut UART: [u8; 8]` → port_io (x86: COM1, AArch64: PL011), `.mmio.0x..` → mmio, `.port.0x3f8` → port_io, `.fb.0x..` → #[framebuffer] mmio, `arena!` / `bump_arena!` / `port_io!` / `mmio!` / `own_alloc!`, `println!` formatting, removal of `unsafe` / `pub` / `use` / `extern "C"` / `#[no_mangle]` / `#![no_std]`, char literals and lifetimes, `while let`, `-> !`, `#[panic_handler]`. All meaning is checked by the rules of Fascon (generation tags, bounds checks, own).
constraints: impl blocks, traits, generics and closures are not rewritten (errors under the rules of Fascon).

name: --emit-strict-fascon
summary: writes the strict Fascon form for functional-safety review
detail: Writes <out dir>/<name>.strict.fsc with the type of every let, typed integer literals, generation-verified lookups (writes `.get_mut(i).unwrap()`, reads `.get(i).unwrap()`), port `read` / `write`, expanded type aliases, call-region notes and the reframing record. Compiling it again gives the same C as the original (checked by the tests).

name: 仮想 BIOS
summary: x86_64 and AArch64 BIOS images from one source (fascon bios / fascon qemu --target)
detail: x86_64: an image for QEMU -bios: reset vector (0xFFFF_FFF0) → protected mode → long mode with 0-4 GiB identity-mapped by 2 MiB pages → the kernel image copied to RAM at 1 MiB, then COM1, all 256 interrupt entries, GDT / TSS and ramfb (fw_cfg I/O ports) are set up and main runs. It is multi-core (up to 4 cores started with INIT-SIPI-SIPI, per-core TLS through FS) and has the LAPIC timer (irq 27) and the HPET clock, the I/O APIC (input n is irq 32 + n), ring 3 user processes (`int $0x80`), per-task page tables (CR3 + PCID) and an NMI that stops every core on a panic. AArch64: QEMU virt -bios (flash at 0) copies the kernel image to 0x4008_0000 and enters the BSP (single-core). Neither uses SeaBIOS or UEFI. `fascon bios app.fsc` builds both; `fascon qemu app.fsc --target x86_64 | aarch64` boots one.
constraints: Needs clang + ld.lld (or x86_64 / aarch64 gcc) and qemu-system-x86_64 / qemu-system-aarch64.

name: F0282
summary: a type still unknown is used as the base of a field, a method or an index
detail: Reported only when two type-checking passes could not settle it (usually later assignments and calls do).
remedy: Write one type on that let.

name: F2401
summary: bump_arena slots are not freed one by one (released together, in O(1), when the call region returns)
detail: A slot of a bump_arena was freed one by one with `free` / `remove`. A bump_arena is rewound all at once, in O(1), when its call region returns.
remedy: Keep values freed one by one in an `arena`.

name: F2402
summary: an Id of a bump_arena stored where it would outlive its call region (table elements, statics)
detail: When the call region returns the Id becomes invalid by generation and top (still safe at run time, but storing it is pointless, so it is reported at compile time).
remedy: Make the target an `arena` when its Ids are stored for long.

name: F2205
summary: invalid port_io declaration (elements u8 / u16 / u32, ports 0 to 0xFFFF)
detail: A `port_io` declaration has the wrong shape: the type is not u8 / u16 / u32 or an array of them (x86 in / out are 8, 16 or 32 bits), or the range does not fit the I/O space (0 to 0xFFFF).
remedy: Match the element width and port numbers to the device. Write memory-mapped registers as `mmio`.

name: F2304
summary: own_alloc(T) would need an endless chain of own children
detail: own_alloc creates the non-Option own children zero-filled, so an own path leading back to the type never ends.
remedy: Make the own on the way back `Option<own T>` (it starts as None).

name: irq 名前 at INTID { .. }
summary: An interrupt handler item
detail: The body runs as a closed section (interrupts masked). The compiler emits a table of INTIDs and handlers; the BSP enables, acknowledges and ends the interrupt. This is not the 0.1 `#[isr]` syntax. INTIDs 16 to 31 are per-core interrupts (the timer is 27) and 32 and up are peripheral interrupts delivered to CPU0. On the x86_64 virtual BIOS the LAPIC timer is 27 and input n of the I/O APIC is 32 + n, so the same source runs on both.
constraints: No parameters or result. INTIDs are 16 to 1019 and distinct (F2602). The body cannot call anything that may switch tasks (F2603). On multi-core, handlers of peripheral interrupts (32 and up) cannot touch per-core arenas (F2616).
remedy: Request a switch on interrupt exit with `@task.resume(next)`.

name: 環境効果 E_env
summary: The effects of the other execution roots, assumed to happen at every point that can be interrupted
detail: E(f) ranges over arenas (task_arena and bump_arena included). In an open section the union of the effects of the interrupt handlers (and of the other tasks in preemptive mode) is assumed to happen, and unprotected access (F2601) is checked against it. On multi-core the effects of every root on other cores (task, syscall, irq) are added (per-core arenas excluded). A call that may switch (`yield_to`, `exit`) is treated as a call carrying the effects of every execution root, so borrows (F2502) and the expiry of liveness proofs follow the existing rules. MMIO and ports are not checked, and heap allocation and release are closed inside the runtime.
constraints: The mode (cooperative or preemptive) is decided by the compiler: preemptive if an irq handler calls `resume`.

name: --target rtos
summary: the bare-metal embedded profile (32-bit Ids, fixed .fascon_arena, no recursion)
detail: Compiling unchanged sources with `--target rtos` (or `// fascon-target: rtos` at the top of the file) keeps 32-bit Ids [generation 32-K | index K] and arenas in .fascon_arena (2 MiB aligned, fixed size, up to 16,777,216 slots). A cycle in the call graph (function-pointer candidates included) is F3001. `fascon stack` computes the maximum stack use from the C call graph (GCC -fcallgraph-info=su) and compares it with a limit.
constraints: No recursion (use a loop with an explicit stack).
remedy: `fascon stack app.fsc --target rtos --limit 8192`

name: --target generic-os
summary: the general multi-process OS profile (64-bit Ids, VA-reserved arenas, per-CPU magazines, RCU, PAC / BTI, Spectre masking)
detail: The same source gets `f20_id_t = uint64_t` (upper 32 = generation, lower 32 = index, 0ULL = None) with colouring (F2101) unchanged. alloc / free of shared arenas are lock-free per-CPU magazines (allowed outside critical) and frees are reclaimed after an RCU grace period. Indices derived from outside data get the Spectre v1 mask + CSDB, function pointers are signed with PACIA and authenticated with AUTIA before calls, callback candidates start with BTI c, and mmio goes through a high virtual mirror (virtual 0-2 MiB is an unmapped guard).
constraints: Pass raw Ids as `IdRaw` (u32 on rtos, u64 on generic-os).
remedy: `fascon run app.fsc --target generic-os` / `// fascon-target: generic-os`

name: Result<T, E>
summary: a success value T or a failure E (E copyable; usually FaultError)
detail: Built with `Ok(v)` / `Err(e)` and used with `Ok(x)` / `Err(e)` patterns, `e?` (an early return of the same form on failure), `is_ok()`, `is_err()`, `unwrap()` and `unwrap_or(v)`. In C an {is_some, value, err} struct. Angle-bracket types are only this, `Option<T>` and `Id<a>` (no generics are added).
constraints: `?` applies only to a Result, inside a function returning a Result (F3105).

name: catch_fault
summary: an expression catching latched faults, user-memory faults and failed unwraps inside as Result<T, FaultError>
detail: `let r = catch_fault { .. };`. Commit points inside jump locally to the handler instead of stopping (no non-local exit), dropping the values made in the section first. Functions called from the section move their latch into a per-core pending word and return; the caller takes it in. Faults map to errno values (stale Id → ESTALE, overflow → EOVERFLOW, user memory → EFAULT, outside a device window → EIO).
constraints: Outer values cannot be moved inside (F3106).

name: user T
summary: a user-space buffer (`user [u8; N]` / `user Str`), only as a #[syscall(N)] parameter
detail: The kernel cannot read the contents directly (F3101). `copy_from_user(ubuf)?` copies once onto the kernel stack (fixed size) or into own [u8; limit] (user Str), and a second read is F3101 too (no TOCTOU). The length of a user Str is checked against the limit (4096 by default, limits.user_str_max in board.toml) before copying; beyond it, EFAULT without copying and the latch F20_FAULT_USER. `copy_to_user(ubuf, &kbuf)?` writes back. On generic-os AArch64 the copies use LDTR / STTR with PAN = 1 and an exception table (.ex_table).
constraints: Receive a struct as user [u8; N] and read the copy with `.read(T, 0)` (F3102).

name: #[syscall(N)]
summary: a system call entry (the attribute form); the compiler builds the number check, the table and per-type register validation
detail: `#[syscall(0)] fn sys_read(fd: u32, ubuf: user [u8; 256]) -> Result<usize, FaultError>`. AArch64 uses SVC #0 (x8 = number), x86_64 SYSCALL. The entry checks integer ranges, bools (0 / 1), Ids (validate; forged → EBADF) and user T ranges (EFAULT) before calling the body. Ok(v) gives x0 = v, Err(e) x0 = -errno. A latched fault in the body does not stop the kernel but becomes Err(errno).
constraints: Returns Result<integer or (), FaultError> or i64 (F3104). The 1.0 `syscall .. at N` form cannot take user T or bool (F3103).

name: #[trap]
summary: EL0 page-fault handling `#[trap] fn user_fault(pid: Id<table>, addr: u64, is_write: bool)`
detail: The entry builds the arguments from (ESR, FAR, PC) (pid is the Id of the running task, validated, is_write the WnR bit of the ESR). The body has a _flt latch of its own; Sleep calls are F3203. Copy-on-Write is written with own [u8; 4096] moves only: `procs.cow_copy(pid, va)` copies into a fresh own page, `procs.map_page(pid, va, page, true)` swaps it in with ownership, and `procs.tlb_flush(pid, va)` picks a local TLBI or IPIs from cpu_mask.
constraints: Another shape is F3204.

name: atomic
summary: one indivisible read-modify-write of an integer (or bool) field of one slot
detail: `atomic { t[id].f |= 1; }` (statement) / `let old = atomic { t[id].n += 1 };` (the value form without `;` yields the old value; = is an exchange) / `atomic { t[id].f }` (a load). On AArch64 one LSE LDADDAL / LDSETAL / SWPAL / LDAR. Overflow of += / -= latches. Reductions involving fields updated under atomic or #[no_column] fields fall back to the phase-1 scan without columns instead of failing (the reason shows in fascon regions).
constraints: Calls, loops, several slots or statements are F3201 (use critical).

name: rcu_read
summary: a read-only section with preemption disabled (an RCU reader)
detail: Only &T reads inside. Writes, allocations, frees and calls of functions doing them are F3202; sleeping calls are F3203. On generic-os a free of a shared arena keeps the generation bump and the slot reuse in a deferred queue until a grace period (the epoch of every core advances twice), so a slot a reader holds is not rewritten before it is done (no ABA).
constraints: Each field reads old or new; to publish several fields consistently, build a new slot and swap the Id in with atomic.

name: Sleep 効果
summary: the mark of functions that may sleep (schedule, sleep_ticks, rcu_synchronize, #[sleep], #[asm(effects = "sleep")], and blocking operations)
detail: Computed as a transitive closure over the call graph. Calling one inside rcu_read / atomic / #[trap], or while a second-class reference is live, is F3203 (another task could free the target while this one sleeps). On preemption the TCB saves and restores the general registers (including the _flt latch), the frame-region position and the catch_fault pending latch.

name: #[secret]
summary: a secret value (a key ...): no copies, output or secret-dependent branches; volatile zeroing on drop
detail: On structs, fields and `#[secret] let`. Copies into non-secret places, passing by value and output are F3301; secret-dependent if / match / while / comparisons / && / indices are F3302 (use the constant-time `ct_eq(&a, &b)`); asm operands are F3303; mismatched ct_eq types are F3304. Every drop path runs fascon_secure_zero (volatile stores + an asm taking the address + a barrier: never removed by DSE). With #[on_drop] the order is 1. on_drop → 2. zeroing + barrier → 3. free.

name: dma own T
summary: an owned value shared with a device (its own 4 KiB-aligned pages; never embedded)
detail: Made with `dma_alloc(T)`; `submit_dma(buf)` lends it (the value is gone, an IOVA comes back; later use is F3401) and `complete_dma(T, iova)` returns Option<dma own T> (forged IOVAs and double completions are None). Lending cleans with DC CVAC + DSB SY, returning invalidates with DC IVAC + DSB SY, and generic-os maps / unmaps the IOVA in the IOMMU (Arm SMMU / Intel VT-d). A struct field is Option<dma own T> (detached with .take(); a bare one is F3402). T must be POD (F3403).

name: bind_mmio
summary: bind a register struct of a device found by bus enumeration (DTB / ACPI / PCIe): `bind_mmio(Regs, addr)`
detail: Takes a type name first (no generics). Inside a registered device window (board.toml [[device]], a DTB reg, a PCIe BAR) it returns the high virtual mirror, and field / index accesses are volatile (the same guarantees as fixed-address mmio). Outside, it diverts to a window that reads all-ones and drops writes, and latches (EIO under catch_fault). Regs must be a register struct (F3404).

name: extern "C"
summary: the C boundary (import `extern "C" fn f(..) -> T;` / export `extern "C" fn f(..) { .. }`)
detail: Integers, bool, Id, Option<Id> and FaultError cross (F3601). Raw Ids from C (uint32_t on rtos, uint64_t on generic-os) get a validate inserted by the compiler; generation 0, out-of-range indices and non-canonical values become None.

name: #[asm(..)]
summary: the safe inline-assembly boundary `#[asm(aarch64 = "..", x86_64 = "..", host = "..", effects = "..")] fn f(..) -> T;`
detail: Operands are integers or bool only (nothing pointing to memory: F3503) and never #[secret] values (F3303). effects (none / sleep / barrier / irq / mmio) enter the effect analysis; sleep gives the Sleep effect. {r} is the result, {name} / {index} the arguments. PC runs use the host C expression.
aliases: インラインアセンブリ

name: #[on_drop(f)] / #[no_column] / #[stable_abi]
summary: attributes for writing libraries: a drop hook, fields without columns, a fixed layout
detail: #[on_drop(f)]: calls `fn f(x: &mut S)` first when the value is dropped (another shape is F3505; it cannot sleep). #[no_column]: a write-heavy field; reductions involving it get no columns. #[stable_abi]: declaration order, natural C alignment, no columns; fields are integers, bool, arrays of them, wire structs or other #[stable_abi] structs only (F3502). For dynamically loaded drivers and IPC boundaries. An Id<@a> changes width between rtos (32 bits) and generic-os (64 bits), so it cannot be placed directly (F3501; pass a u64 across and validate it back).

name: import
summary: module import `import net::tcp;` (used as `tcp::connect(..)`)
detail: Searched in the folder of this file → fsc_modules/ (`fascon pkg add`) → FASCON_PATH → lib/ next to the executable → the embedded standard library. Items are renamed to `net_tcp__connect` / `Net_Tcp__Conn` (namespaces without lifetimes or generics). Modules are checked in parallel and passing ones are cached by content hash in .fascon-cache/. Not found is F3701, an error inside a module F3702, an alias clash F3703 (`import a::b as c;`).

name: fascon pkg
summary: the package manager (fascon.toml [dependencies] into fsc_modules/)
detail: `fascon pkg init` / `new <name>` / `add <name> --path <dir>` / `add <name> --git <url> [--rev r]` / `install` / `list` / `std`. fascon.lock records what was installed and a content hash. Standard library: sync::spinlock, sync::mutex, collections::vec, time::wheel, sched::hmp, net::wire, net::udp, net::tcp, fs::pagecache, fs::cowfs, ipc::rpc, loader::elf, pm::power.

name: board.toml
summary: a declarative board definition (memory map, interrupt controller, timer, UART, device windows)
detail: `--board boards/qemu-virt-aarch64.toml`. [board] name / arch / profile / cpus, [memory] ram_base / ram_size, [uart] kind / base, [irq] kind / gicd / gicc / gicr, [timer] intid / hz, [[device]] name / base / size, [limits] user_str_max / dma_pool_pages, [vm] mmio_mirror / arena_va_base, [cpu] big = [..]. fascon_board.h is written next to the generated C and read by both the BSP and the generated C. Errors are F3801.

name: F3001
summary: recursion under `--target rtos`
detail: A cycle in the call graph (function-pointer candidates included); the maximum stack use could not be proven.
remedy: Use a loop with an explicit stack.

name: F3010 / F3011
summary: the raw Id width on generic-os (warning) / generic-os-only operations
detail: F3010: validate on generic-os got an integer narrower than 64 bits (no room for the generation, always None). F3011: address-space / TLB operations used outside generic-os.
remedy: Use IdRaw / pass --target generic-os.

name: F3105
summary: misuse of Result and `?`
detail: `?` on a non-Result, in a function not returning a Result, or a non-copyable Result error type.
remedy: Handle Options with if let and `return Err(EINVAL);`.

name: F3401 / F3402 / F3403 / F3404
summary: the rules of DMA and MMIO
detail: F3401: a value used by the CPU while lent (submit_dma to complete_dma). F3402: a bare dma own field. F3403: a value shared with a device is not POD. F3404: the type of bind_mmio / mmio T is not a register struct.
remedy: Use the value taken back by complete_dma / use Option<dma own T> / use integers, arrays and wire structs only.

name: F3503 / F3504 / F3601 / F3801
summary: errors in boundary types, attributes and board definitions
detail: F3503: a malformed #[asm] (shape, operands, effects). F3504 (warning): an unknown attribute. F3601: a type that cannot cross extern "C". F3801: board.toml cannot be read or misses a required key.
remedy: F3503: follow the shape, operands and effects of the examples in `fascon dict #[asm(..)]`. F3504: fix the spelling of the attribute (it is a warning, so the build continues). F3601: use integers, bool, Id, `Option<Id>` or FaultError as extern "C" parameters and results (incoming Ids are validated). F3801: follow the syntax and required keys of the example in `fascon dict board.toml`.

name: gc_arena
summary: an arena reclaimed by fascon-gc (deterministic, precise GC)
detail: `gc_arena nodes: Node[N];` (`shared gc_arena` for one instance on every core). Elements are named by Id<nodes> (coloured types; F2101, F0515 and F0520 apply unchanged). gc_collect(nodes) marks by reading only the type descriptors (.rodata), the live bitmaps and the Id-only projection columns, and sweeps live & ~mark with ctz / blsr. Dead slots go to the free of the arena (own drop, zero fill, generation + 1, column unmirror, free list / magazine; shared arenas after an RCU grace period). Roots are statics, slots of ordinary arena / bump_arena, the shadow stack (locals and parameters holding gc Ids) and suspended tasks.
constraints: manual free / remove is F2621; allocation and gc_collect inside #[trap], rcu_read, atomic, critical or irq is F2622; F2623 with --gc=off; dma own T in the element is F2624; Ids of a shared gc_arena in a per-core arena are F2625. Collections happen at gc_collect statements (and, for shared gc_arena, at loop-head and waiting safepoints). Temporaries in the middle of an expression are roots too (gc Ids evaluated before an expression that may collect are moved by the compiler into temporaries registered on the shadow stack until the end of the statement). For channels that can carry Ids of a shared gc_arena, elements sent but not yet received are read as roots.
remedy: drop the references and the next gc_collect reclaims the slots; when alloc returns None, gc_collect and retry.
aliases: ガベージコレクション

name: promote_to_gc
summary: copy a bump_arena survivor into a gc_arena (generational evacuation)
detail: `promote_to_gc(nodes, bump_id)` gives Option<Id<nodes>>. Build temporaries in a bump_arena in O(1) and copy only what survives; the rest vanishes with one rewind at function exit. Automatic promotion by escape analysis: passing a bump_arena Id where a gc_arena Id of the same element type is expected (a return value, argument, field or typed let) makes the compiler insert promote_to_gc.
constraints: the element types must match (bump_arena elements cannot hold own).

name: F2621 / F2622 / F2623 / F2624 / F2625
summary: fascon-gc errors
detail: F2621: free / remove on a gc_arena (freeing is the job of the GC). F2622: allocation, gc_collect or promote_to_gc on a gc_arena inside #[trap], rcu_read, atomic, critical or an irq handler (functions called from there included) (unbounded time; waiting for parked cores could deadlock). F2623: gc_arena with --gc=off (FASCON_GC=off; a fully deterministic build that links no GC runtime). F2624: dma own T in a gc_arena element (could be reclaimed mid-transfer). F2625: an Id of a shared gc_arena in a per-core arena (a root the collecting core cannot see). F2601-F2604 of the specification already mean other things in Fascon 1.0, so they live at F2621-F2624 with the same last digit.
remedy: F2621: delete the free / remove and leave reclaiming to gc_collect (a Quick Fix does it). F2622: move allocation and collection out of closed sections, irq handlers, #[trap], rcu_read and atomic (into the open sections of ordinary tasks). F2623: drop `--gc=off`, or make the gc_arena an ordinary arena. F2624: keep dma own T in an ordinary arena, not a gc_arena. F2625: keep Ids of a shared gc_arena in shared arenas (shared arena / shared gc_arena).

name: Pure Safe / Low-Level / Hardware
summary: the safety labels of fascon pkg
detail: fascon pkg label (and fascon pkg install, and fascon build inside a package) scans every source of the package and writes safety and safety_reasons into [package] of fascon.toml: Pure Safe with no #[asm], no extern "C" and no hardware boundary (mmio, port_io, bind_mmio, dma, irq, #[trap], #[syscall], user_mem, volatile_bypass); otherwise Low-Level / Hardware with the reasons and places. fascon.lock carries the label of each dependency.

name: hal::console / hal::timer / hal::block / hal::net
summary: the standard HAL (structs of function pointers)
detail: Console { putc, getc, flush }, Timer { now_ns, freq_hz, arm_oneshot, cancel }, BlockDevice { sectors, read, write, flush }, NetDevice { mac, mtu, send, recv, link_up }. Board packages fill them in (console() in board_hal.fsc, ...), and upper libraries only take &Console and friends, so they run unchanged on another board.

name: board.toml [boot] / --board
summary: a real-hardware image from board.toml alone
detail: With load_addr, stack_size, smp (spin-table / psci-hvc / psci-smc / ipi / none), release_addrs, exit (loop / psci / semihosting) and entry_el in [boot], fascon build --board <name> builds an ELF and a raw .img (straight onto flash or an SD card) with the generic BSP (a start.S that drops to EL1 from EL3 / EL2 / EL1, bsp.c and a generated linker script). [dma] coherent = false adds per-cache-line clean / invalidate, and bus_offset gives the address devices see (bus_addr). A board is added without touching the compiler by putting board.toml and pure-Fascon drivers (board_hal.fsc, ...) in boards/<name>/, plus start.S, bsp.c and [toolchain] when needed (RISC-V, ...). fascon qemu --board boots it on [qemu] machine.

name: fascon_plat_*
summary: The CPU-independent functions generated C calls (each board BSP implements them)
detail: The C the compiler emits contains no CPU-specific instruction and calls only these functions declared in `runtime/fascon2_rt.h`: interrupts and locks (`irq_save` / `irq_restore` / `irq_open` / `wait_irq`, `critical_enter` / `critical_exit`), the clock (`timer_now` / `timer_freq` / `timer_arm`), tasks (`task_create` / `task_create_user` / `task_enter` / `task_yield` / `task_resume` / `task_exit` / `task_current`), multi-core (`spawn_on` / `cpu_count` / `cpu_id`), address spaces (`vm_space` / `vm_map` / `vm_unmap` / `vm_switch` / `vm_flush` / `vm_drop`), user space (`user_register` / `user_window` / `copy_from_user` / `copy_to_user` / `syscall_register` / `trap_register`), panics (`panic_broadcast` / `core_parked`) and fascon-gc (`gc_task_tops`). Implementations: bsp/qemu-virt-aarch64 and bsp/qemu-x86_64-bios (everything), bsp/generic-aarch64 and boards/qemu-virt-riscv64 (interrupts, clock, core count), bsp/portable-stub (the porting template) and bsp/host (PC execution).
constraints: Interrupt controllers, page tables and TLB instructions live only in the BSPs, never in the compiler (src/*.rs).
remedy: For a new board, write these functions in C under `boards/<name>/` and describe it in `board.toml` (the compiler is not touched). `python3 tools/cross_check.py target/release/fascon` checks that generated C compiles with `-Werror` and links for five architectures.

name: f32 / f64
summary: IEEE-754 floating-point numbers (single and double precision); by default operations run in written order, bit for bit
detail: Literals are `1.5`, `2.0f32`, `1e-3`; without a suffix the type is inferred (f64 when undecided). Arithmetic is plain IEEE-754 (contraction into FMA is turned off in the C), `as` to integers saturates (NaN gives 0), and `put(x)` prints the shortest decimal that reads back (the shape of `{:?}` in Rust). Value methods are `to_bits()`, `is_nan()`, `is_finite()` and `abs()`, plus `f32::from_bits(u)` / `f64::from_bits(u)` and constants such as `f64::INFINITY`, `f64::NAN` and `f64::EPSILON`. Reductions are parallelized (reassociated) only under `#[fast_math]`.
constraints: Floats cannot be wire struct fields (F2701). `==` is the IEEE-754 comparison (NaN equals nothing, itself included).
remedy: Compare bit patterns with `x.to_bits() == y.to_bits()`.

name: #[fast_math]
summary: an attribute that lets a loop or function reassociate its float reductions into parallel lanes and use columns
detail: Sums and filtered sums such as `#[fast_math] for id in @a { s += @a[id].x; }` read f32 / f64 True-SoA columns (float / double) with four independent vector accumulators (f20_col_sum_f32 / _f64, _m when filtered). Min / max picks use IEEE-754 order-preserving key columns (F20_KEY_F32 / F20_KEY_F64: sign bit 0 flips the sign bit, 1 flips every bit; NaN is never picked; -0.0 compares as +0.0). Loops without the attribute keep the written order, bit for bit. `--fast-math` (FASCON_FAST_MATH=1) applies it to the whole program.
constraints: The last digits of a sum may differ from the written-order sum (lanes are added separately, then combined).
remedy: Leave it off reductions that must match bit for bit; `--columns off` returns to scans without columns.

name: 完全列化（True SoA）
summary: tables whose fields read by reductions leave the slot and live only in a column (one write per update)
detail: With `--columns on` (the default) a field that reductions read and that is never referenced as a whole element or by address becomes True SoA (single-write): `@a[id].f` reads and writes the column `ts_f[i]` instead of the slot. Mirror columns (Mirrored-SoA, dual-write) remain only for columns built from fields kept in the slot, such as filter bit columns and key columns. Bulk overwrites of columns of 8 MiB or more use non-temporal stores (F20_NT_STORE and F20_SFENCE at the exit). Write-heavy fields (write weight above scan weight) get no mirror columns. `fascon regions` shows the decision and the reasons per table.
constraints: Fields under #[stable_abi], #[wire], the extern "C" boundary or whose address is taken stay in the slot (regions names the reason).
remedy: `--columns mirrored` keeps mirror columns only, `--columns off` gives the 1.0.0 tables, `--nontemporal off` turns non-temporal stores off.

name: 条件付き一括更新（Masked Column RMW）
summary: turns `for id in @a { if cond { @a[id].f += x / = x } }` into a branch-free vector update that reads the filter bit column word by word
detail: When f is a True-SoA column (u32, u64, i32, i64; f32 and f64 under #[fast_math]), the condition fits a filter bit column and x does not change in the loop (a literal, local, static or constant), f20_col_masked_add_* / f20_col_masked_set_* process 64 slots at a time: zero words are skipped without touching the column lines, all-one words use an unmasked vector operation (non-temporal stores at 8 MiB or more), the rest a predicated operation with the bits spread over the lanes, in place. Integer adds check every lane for overflow; an overflowing word is restored and the sequential loop continues from it (the same panic at the same place).
constraints: Shared arenas, tables shared with interrupts or tasks, and dma / gpu / gc / bump / task arenas are not eligible.
remedy: The masked column RMW lines of `fascon regions` list the column, bit column, kernel and store kind; `--columns off` returns to the sequential loop.

name: gpu_arena / GpuBuf<@g> / GpuFence<@g>
summary: a table whose slots are lent to an accelerator (GPU / NPU); handles are move-only and completion is checked with tickets
detail: `gpu_arena @g: T[N];` lives on a 2 MiB boundary in .bss.fascon_gpu (pinnable pages). `@g.alloc(v)` returns `Option<GpuBuf<@g>>`, and the CPU may use `@g[h]` only while it holds the handle. `@g.dispatch(kernel, grid, block, h)` consumes h (later use is F0382) and returns a ticket `GpuFence<@g>`. `@g.reclaim(f)` returns the handle once the work is done (no waiting); `@g.reclaim_wait(f)` waits for it (the Sleep effect: F2603 in critical and irq, F3203 in rcu_read). A second reclaim with the same ticket gives None. The generated C calls only fascon_plat_gpu_register / dispatch / poll / wait; on the PC a worker thread runs the FASCON_GPU_KERNEL(id) functions of `<name>.gpu.c`.
constraints: Elements are plain old data (integers, floats and arrays / structs of them; F2705). It cannot be iterated and has no Id-based operations (F2706).
remedy: `--gpu=off` (FASCON_GPU=off) offloads nothing; dispatch runs in place on the calling core (warning F2707).

name: --target hpc
summary: the HPC / compute node profile (64-bit Ids, 2 MiB-aligned arenas, pinning to physical cores, NUMA-local binding)
detail: `--target hpc` or `// fascon-target: hpc`. Ids are 64 bits [generation 32 | index 32] and every table sits on a 2 MiB boundary (MADV_HUGEPAGE on the PC). Once at main and at each spawn_on entry, fascon_plat_pin_core pins the core to a physical core (avoiding SMT siblings) and fascon_plat_numa_bind binds the per-core arenas, fascon__cpu[core] and the own heap to that core NUMA node (MPOL_BIND). `#[numa_node(n)]` picks the node of a shared table. The compute node shape comes from `--topology cores=N,smt=K,numa=M` or `// fascon-topology: ..` (default cores=128 smt=2 numa=8). F3901 to F3903 keep the management core (0) and the compute cores (1..N) apart.
constraints: Pinning and binding are advisory and never stop the program (FASCON_HPC_NO_PIN turns them off). `#[no_smt]` goes on fn main.
remedy: The HPC section of `fascon regions` lists each core role, physical core and NUMA node, and the functions reachable from compute cores.

name: F2705
summary: the element of a gpu_arena is not plain old data
detail: The device reads and writes the slot bytes as they are. own, Id, Str, references, function pointers, bool and Option point into other tables or heaps, or become broken values from device-written bits, so they are not allowed. Allowed are integers, floats and arrays / structs of them (not necessarily wire structs).
remedy: Keep CPU-side data (Id, own, Str) in an ordinary arena and link it by the index `h.index()`; if nothing is offloaded, make it an ordinary `arena`.

name: F2706
summary: misuse of gpu_arena handles and tickets (another table, the wrong type, for, Id operations)
detail: `GpuBuf<@g>` and `GpuFence<@g>` work only with the gpu_arena they came from. One of: a handle of another gpu_arena passed to dispatch / free / `@g[h]`, an integer or a handle passed to reclaim instead of a ticket, a table that is not a gpu_arena named in `GpuBuf<..>`, a gpu_arena iterated with for (some slots may be on the device), or an Id operation such as get, contains or validate.
remedy: Handles come from alloc and reclaim, tickets from dispatch. Keep the handles in a table of your own (an arena or an array) and iterate that; write `Id<@a>` for the Id of an ordinary table.

name: F2707
summary: a gpu_arena is used with `--gpu=off` (warning)
detail: With `--gpu=off` (FASCON_GPU=off) nothing is offloaded: dispatch runs the C function registered with FASCON_GPU_KERNEL(id) in place on the calling core (nothing when none is registered) and completes at once. The generated C calls no fascon_plat_gpu_* hook.
remedy: Drop `--gpu=off` to offload; a table used by the CPU only can be an ordinary `arena`.

name: F3901
summary: external I/O reachable from a compute-core root (a --target hpc warning)
detail: A function started with `spawn_on(k, ..)` (k > 0, or a core chosen at run time) reaches MMIO, I/O ports, dma, bind_mmio, submit_dma or gpu_dispatch / reclaim. That is OS / I/O noise on the compute core (interrupts, waits, cache pollution). The HPC section of `fascon regions` lists it too.
remedy: Leave device, DMA and GPU traffic to the management core (core 0) and talk to compute cores through a chan or a shared arena; if it is intended, put `#[allow(hpc_io)]` on the function or the root.

name: F3902
summary: dynamic allocation or a table-wide column mirror rebuild on a compute core (--target hpc)
detail: A path reachable from a compute-core root uses own, own_alloc, gc_arena allocations, promote_to_gc, gc_collect or dma_alloc (page faults and jitter), or writes, inside `for id in @a` (functions its body calls included), a field read by a Mirrored-SoA column (a filter bit column, a key column, ...) and so rebuilds the mirror table-wide (which columns are mirrors is decided by code generation, so that part is checked afterwards).
remedy: Allocate on the management core before computing and hand data over as an `own` argument, a shared arena or a chan. For mirrors, remove the reason shown by `fascon regions` so the field becomes True SoA, mark it `#[no_column]`, or do table-wide updates on the management core.

name: F3903
summary: a core number or NUMA node beyond the compute node shape, or SMT siblings assigned with #[no_smt] (--target hpc)
detail: A constant spawn_on core number at or above the logical core count, `#[numa_node(n)]` at or above the NUMA node count, or, with `#[no_smt]` on `fn main`, two cores (the management core 0 included) that are sibling threads of one physical core. The shape comes from `--topology`, `// fascon-topology:` or the profile default (cores=128 smt=2 numa=8), in that order. Siblings are c and c + the physical core count by default (adjacent with layout=adjacent).
remedy: Pick cores and nodes the compute node has, or set `--topology cores=N,smt=K,numa=M` / `// fascon-topology: ..` to match the machine; with #[no_smt] pick cores that are not siblings.
